children.translated_text: To <s>Bhavānī</s>, skilled in destroying the afflictions brought by <s>Bhava</s> (worldly existence),
to <s>Śāradā</s> (the autumnal one), <s>Sarasvatī</s>, seated upon the white lion-throne — we bow!
Without heeding the teacher's words, she thoroughly breaks open all knots;
she reveals the ultimate secret — victorious is one's own power of discernment (<s>vimarśa-śakti</s>)!
To Him whose form is infinite consciousness alone, unlimited by direction, time, and the rest,
whose sole measure is self-experience — homage to that tranquil radiance!
In the act of the world's creation and dissolution,
whose effort is the mere play of opening and closing [of the eyes],
of whose fluttering eyelashes with restless glances
they speak — to that Supreme One, to <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, homage!
Homage to the cause of the origin, maintenance, and destruction of the three worlds,
to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the bridge for crossing to the far shore of the boundless ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>!
Whose feet are illuminated by the splendor of the crest-jewels of gods and <s>asuras</s>,
homage to <s>Hari</s>, the Lord of the three worlds, in the form of a lion (<s>Narasiṃha</s>)!
Homage to that <s>Varāha</s> (Boar) who effortlessly lifts the Earth,
in the hollow of whose hoof even <s>Meru</s> becomes a mere hoof-print!
Homage to <s>Śaṃbhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), beautiful with the moon as a crest-ornament kissing his lofty head,
who is the foundation-pillar for the construction of the city of the three worlds!
Who is worshipped even by the gods for the accomplishment of desired goals —
to that remover of all obstacles, the Lord of the <s>Gaṇas</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>), homage!
Women of languid gait from heavy hips, with full and upraised breasts —
homage to that <s>Manmatha</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>), whose temples are women!
Of infinite names, the ordainer of all forms,
expressible by all <s>mantras</s>, the sole lord of the universe — homage!
Oṃ! Homage to <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, the Supreme Self, whose sole form is the highest reality,
who is undivided by the unreal distinctions manifested by His own will!
Whose petal is the mountain-range, whose seed-vessel is the full golden mountain (<s>Meru</s>),
whose stalk is the infinite — homage to Him who sits upon the lotus-seat (<s>Brahmā</s>)!
Just as gold in golden ornaments and water in oceans and the like,
undivided in the divided — to that Supreme Radiance, homage!
Homage to <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, whose greatness transcends speech and mind,
who is the form of the formless, though possessed of the three <s>guṇas</s>, eight <s>guṇas</s>, and infinite <s>guṇas</s>!
Homage to <s>Śiva</s>, who is endowed with the complete pacification of all afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>),
the cutter of the bonds of existence, whose knot of the three <s>guṇas</s> is hard to pierce!
The very absence of all defining marks is itself His distinguishing mark —
homage to that God, that certain indefinable <s>Śaṃbhu</s>!
The sole cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and the sole opponent of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
homage to <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, who is the very form of <s>saṃsāra</s> and yet free from <s>saṃsāra</s>!

children.text: yathā tathāpi yaḥ pūjyo yatra tatrāpi yorcitaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who is worthy of worship howsoever, and wherever He is honored,

children.text: yopi vā sopi vā yosau devastasmai namostu te //
children.translated_text: whoever He may be — to that God, whoever He is, homage to You!

children.text: sadasattvena bhāvānāṃ yuktā yā dvitayī sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: The twofold state of things as existent and non-existent —
transcending that, homage to the wondrous <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, the Third!
Homage to Him whose own glory is stamped with the autonomous power of consciousness (<s>cit-śakti</s>),
whose form is both unmanifest and manifest — to that certain <s>mantra</s>-embodiment!
Near and yet far away, hidden and yet openly manifest,
easily accessible and yet most difficult to attain — homage to the wondrous <s>Śaṃbhu</s>!
Whose nature is the very shining-forth of the vast, moving and unmoving world,
whose secret is hard to fathom even by the adept — homage to that Self!

children.text: viṣṇurvā tripurāntako bhavatu vā brahmā surendrothavā
children.translated_text: Whether it be <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or the Destroyer of the Three Cities (<s>Śiva</s>), or <s>Brahmā</s>, or the king of the gods (<s>Indra</s>),
or the Sun, or the Moon-marked One, or the glorious <s>Buddha</s>, or the <s>Siddha</s> (<s>Jina</s>),
whoever is free from passion, hatred, suffering of poison, and delusion, and strives with compassion for beings,

children.text: yaḥ sarvaiḥ saha saṃskṛto guṇaguṇaistasmai namaḥ sarvadā //
children.translated_text: and is endowed with all good qualities — to that one, always, homage!
This verse is attributed to <s>Svāmidatta</s>; for his remembrance it is marked in the poetry;
it was composed by one whose name bears the syllable 'ka' among poets, called <s>Cakrapāṇi</s>.
He in whom the seeds and sprouts of existence — passion and the rest — that are rain-clouds have been destroyed,

children.text: brahmā vā viṣṇurvā haro jino vā namastasmai //
children.translated_text: whether He be <s>Brahmā</s>, or <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), or the <s>Jina</s> — homage to Him!
A <s>kastūrī</s> (musk) mark on the forehead, the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem on the chest,

children.text: nāsāgre navamauktikaṃ karatale veṇuṃ kare kaṅkaṇam /
children.translated_text: a fresh pearl on the tip of the nose, a flute in the palm, a bracelet on the wrist,

children.text: sarvāṅge haricandanaṃ suvimalaṃ kaṇṭhe ca muktāvalīṃ
children.translated_text: pure <s>haricandana</s> (sandalwood) paste on every limb, and a string of pearls on the throat —
wearing all this, surrounded by women, victorious shines <s>Gopāla</s>, the crest-jewel of cowherds!
May the body of <s>Brahmā</s>, with its body-hair standing erect in the joy of constantly radiating knowledge,
appearing as if covered with thick pollen from constant contact with lotuses, protect you!
May the arm-trees of <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), bright with the beautiful leaf-vine designs transferred from <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s cheeks,
dense in shade and bearing great fruit, protect you!
May the tusk of the Great Boar (<s>Mahāvarāha</s>), a swing for the Earth,
a thief of the moonlight of <s>Bali</s>, and a lamp for the halls of <s>Pātāla</s>, protect you!
He who, mighty in valor, descended into the <s>Yamunā</s> to subdue the maddened, intoxicating serpent (<s>Kāliya</s>) —
may that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the queller of <s>Madana</s>'s humiliation, act for my delight and the delight of the immortals!
May He protect you — He by whom the remaining <s>Daityas</s>,
painted with collyrium of the same dark color as His,
even seeing it applied with brushes, tremble
at the blue lotuses of their own beloved's eyes!
May the body of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, adorned with the shattering of the circle of the fierce arms of <s>Cāṇūra</s>,
protect you — <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the guise of a boy, a wrestler among cowherds!
When, at the lifting of <s>Govardhana</s>, all the cowherds were overjoyed
and praised Him with various hymns, His mind became embarrassed;
remembering His Boar form, with the Earth raised upon His tusk shining like the crescent moon,
may the smile of <s>Hari</s> protect you!
When the ocean's waters, churned by the whirling of <s>Mandara</s> mountain, surged within,
and <s>Lakṣmī</s>, tender as a budding sprout, was about to be crushed, flustered at the emergency,
the words of the Slayer of <s>Madhu</s>, whose skin bristled with delight, eager to cease
the labor of pulling gods and <s>asuras</s> — may they protect the world!
The breaths of the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the form of the Tortoise (<s>Kūrma</s>), drowsy from the scratching of his back
by the edges of the rocks of the great <s>Mandara</s> mountain revolving on his back — may they protect you!
By the force of whose habitual impressions, the coming and going of the waters of the ocean,
tireless, carried by the inertia of the waves, does not rest even to this day.
May the gleam of the teeth of <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) protect you — He who, with eyes slightly closed, drinks one breast,
with one hand wipes away a freshly dripping drop of milk from the other,
while His chin is fondled by His mother's single finger, His face smiling —

children.text: cchaureḥ kṣīrakaṇāvalīva patitā dantadyutiḥ pātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: the gleam of His teeth falling from His face like a string of milk-drops!
While <s>Balarāma</s> (the one with the pestle) has gone to play on the banks of the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>),

children.text: tāvatkarburikāpayaḥ piba hare vardhiṣyate te śikhā /
children.translated_text: 'Drink the spotted cow's milk, O <s>Hari</s>! Your topknot will grow!' —
hearing such coaxing words of <s>Yaśodā</s>, intended to trick Him by His childhood,
may <s>Hari</s>, touching His own topknot in delight while the milk is only half-drunk, protect you!
Seen with joy by <s>Yaśodā</s>, with ardor by the cowherd women, for a long time,
with anxiety by the enemy of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Kaṃsa</s>), with flowers by the <s>Siddhas</s>, with agitation by the earth,

children.text: serṣyaṃ gopakumārakaiḥ sakaruṇaṃ pauraiḥ suraiḥ sasmitaṃ
children.translated_text: with envy by the cowherd boys, with compassion by the citizens, with a smile by the gods —

children.text: yo dṛṣṭaḥ sa punātu vo madhuripuḥ protkṣipragovardhanaḥ //
children.translated_text: He who was thus beheld, may that foe of <s>Madhu</s>, lifting <s>Govardhana</s>, purify you!
'Mother, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> went out to play but now has eaten mud of his own will!'

children.text: satyaṃ kṛṣṇa ka evamāha musalī mithyāmba paśyānanam /
children.translated_text: 'Is that true, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?' 'Who says so?' '<s>Balarāma</s>.' 'It's false, Mother — look at my mouth!'

children.text: vyādehīti vikāsitetha vadane mātā samastaṃ jagad-
children.translated_text: 'Open it!' — and when His mouth was thus opened, His mother, beholding the entire universe

children.text: dṛṣṭvā yasya jagāma vismayavaśaṃ pāyātsa vaḥ keśavaḥ //
children.translated_text: within it, was overcome with wonder — may that <s>Keśava</s> protect you!
'Is it right, pray, to make a thousand wives now, while I, devoted exclusively to You,
a devotee dwelling on Your chest, am cast aside?'
Thus having spoken, seeing her own reflection in the jewel of the serpent's hood and thinking it was herself —
may <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s embarrassed smile at interrupting <s>Hari</s>'s sleep protect you!
Consoling with reverence the beloved queen whose sight He Himself had arranged, when she,
with sidelong glances falling at this spot, was awakened even by tears —

children.text: pratyāyyastvamato mayā nanu hare koyaṃ kramavyatyayaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Yet You are persuaded by me, O <s>Hari</s>; what is this reversal of order?' —
may the shame-producing reply of the Bow-bearer (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) addressed to the woman of <s>Vraja</s> protect you!
The eye of <s>Hari</s> — devoutly bowed in its glance, rivaling the blue lotus,
employed as a support for meditation by those devoted to <s>samādhi</s> for the attainment of well-being,
the great treasure-house of beauty, bestowing the state of being relished upon the eye of <s>Lakṣmī</s> —

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ kurutāṃ bhavārtiharaṇaṃ netre tanurvā hareḥ //
children.translated_text: may the eye or the body of <s>Hari</s> bring about the removal of your worldly suffering!
He by whom the <s>Kāmadeva</s> (god of love) was destroyed, and the body of the conqueror of <s>Bali</s> (<s>Indra</s>) was formerly feminized,
who wears coiling serpents as bracelets and who bore the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: yasyāhuḥ śaśimacchiro hara iti stutyaṃ ca nāmāmarāḥ
children.translated_text: whose praiseworthy name the immortals call 'He who bears the moon on his head, O <s>Hara</s>!' —
may that <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the all-giving one, Himself the destroyer of <s>Andhaka</s> and sin, protect you!
When the clouds of theatrical sleep clear slightly from the face as if from the sky,
outshining with His own brilliance the network of gem-lamp rays from the hoods of the Serpent-King —

children.text: pāyāstāṃ vo muroreḥ śaśitapanamaye locane yadvibhāsā
children.translated_text: may the two eyes of the Slayer of <s>Mura</s>, like sun and moon, protect you — by whose radiance
half of <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s lotus blooms while the other half sinks into sleep!
By the wrestlers seen as a mountain-peak, by all the people as a child, by the flower-bowed women (<s>Apsarases</s>) as <s>Kāma</s>,
by the cowherds as one of ordinary nature, by the thunderbolt-wielding <s>Indra</s> in heaven as the cosmic form beyond measure,
by the enraged <s>Kaṃsa</s> as Death, by the fear-stricken-eyed <s>yogins</s> as the form worthy of meditation —
seen thus at His descent into the arena, may <s>Hari</s>, the bringer of joy to the immortals, protect you!
May the conch of <s>Hari</s>, which splits the hearts of enemies, purify you —
its hollows made resonant by the exhalation of His breath,
as if the seven oceans, residing in the cavern of His belly,
were clashing together with a terrible, thunderous roar!
May the conch of <s>Hari</s>, white as water-lily, jasmine, and lotus-fiber,
a full moon in the sky of His palm, protect you —
by whose sound the girdles of the <s>Asura</s> women
become loose upon their hip-regions!
The form of the <s>Sudarśana</s> discus, seen by <s>Hari</s> at the crest of battle,
its unbearable radiance spreading in all directions —
within the reflection of the sun lodged in its eye,
the discus appears as the disc of the sun — may that protect you!
Severing the throats of the commanders of the rebellious <s>Daitya</s> armies,
its stream reddened with copious blood,
may the discus of <s>Hari</s> grant your desires —
bearing the beauty of the sky made terrible by fires burning in all directions!
Thinking of the discus as an axe for clearing the dense forest of arms — the trees of which are the arrows —
of the rising foe, with its edges scattered by the intense fire's abundant sparks,
when a morsel is about to be swallowed, in the outflow of the fleshy rays of the day-maker (sun),

children.text: muhyatyadyāpi rāhuḥ sa dahatu duritānyāśu daityāntako vaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Rāhu</s> even now swoons — may that Slayer of <s>Daityas</s> burn away your sins!
The claws of <s>Hari</s> in the form of a lion — having found openings by tearing apart the rib-cage of the <s>Daitya</s>,
muddied by the blood-water of the ever-flowing river of blood, become caked with mud,
curved like the tips of the crescent moon, shining like parrot-beaks —
may the claws of <s>Hari</s> in the lion-form protect you!
'Are these ten suns of the dissolution, seizing the expanse of the sky in fear?
Or are these circles of meteors, rising to burn the three worlds?' — thus the terrified
gods exclaimed, beholding the nails of the Bow-bearing <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> (<s>Narasiṃha</s>) form,
reddened with the blood from tearing the chest of the proud <s>Asura</s> — may they protect you!
With <s>Meru</s> as its noble pistil, the vast horizons as its petals,
the hanging, shaking body of <s>Śeṣa</s> as its stalk reaching down to the root,
by whom the blue lotus (<s>Earth</s>) was lifted from the water in play,
as if for a hair-ornament — may that <s>Varāha</s> protect you!
'May the soft Earth not be crushed by the impact of His snout;
may the golden mountain (<s>Meru</s>) not dissolve by the flames from His mouth;

children.text: na śuṣyeyuḥ śvāsaiḥ salilanidhayaḥ sapta ca kathaṃ
children.translated_text: may the seven oceans not dry up from His breaths' —
may that <s>Varāha</s>, accompanied by such a multitude of anxieties, protect you!

children.text: svāmī sanbhuvanatrayasya vikṛtiṃ nītosi kiṃ yācñayā
children.translated_text: 'O Lord of the three worlds, are You reduced to begging?

children.text: yadvā viśvasṛjā tvayaiva na kṛtaṃ taddīyatāṃ te kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or is what was created by You, the Creator, not Yours? Then whence is it to be given to You?

children.text: dānaṃ śreṣṭhatamāya tubhyamatulaṃ bandhāya no muktaye
children.translated_text: This gift to You, the most excellent, is unparalleled — it is for bondage, not liberation!' —

children.text: vijñapto balinā niruttaratayā hrīto hariḥ pātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: silenced thus by <s>Bali</s> with an unanswerable argument, may the embarrassed <s>Hari</s> (<s>Vāmana</s>) protect you!

children.text: līne śrotraikadeśe nabhasi nayanayostejasi kvāpi yāte
children.translated_text: When the sky had merged into one part of an ear, when the light of the eyes had gone somewhere,
when the wind was consumed as an inhalation and a morsel, when the ocean was half-drunk by the lower opening,
seeking the Earth lodged in the gap between one hair on the tip of the snout —
may the magnificence of the Bow-Bearer in Boar form, with objects left unaccounted, purify you!
'Where now are those proud ones, the directional elephants, intoxicated with the fragrance of dense rut-fluid?

children.text: he mero mandarāndre malaya himagire sādhu vaḥ kṣmādharatvam /
children.translated_text: O <s>Meru</s>! O <s>Mandara</s>-king! O <s>Malaya</s>! O <s>Himagiri</s>! How well you bear the name of earth-bearers!'
O <s>Śeṣa</s>, you are praiseworthy with your long heads, those mighty and exuberant ones that bear the weight of the vast world —
thus proclaiming, may the mountain-bearing <s>Varāha</s> (Boar incarnation) protect you!
May <s>Vāmana</s> protect you, in whose <s>Kaustubha</s> gem was reflected
the three worlds, which became like a curious onlooker, as if gazing from within the womb.
'We behold in You, O Lord of life, the entire essence of all the worlds in one place;
O Dark one, upon this body of Yours, the eye of a man of no small merit settles.'
'Whose delight is not in this nectar? Your very glance is nectar!' —
thus addressed by the <s>Daityas</s> as well as by the sages, may <s>Hari</s> in feminine form (<s>Mohinī</s>) protect you!
The revolving great mountain, scratching his back,
afforded him momentary relief from an itch, and he fell into a deep sleep;
with a prolonged, loud, rumbling, terrible snore,
his breath overpowered the ocean — may that Tortoise (<s>Kūrma</s>) protect you!
May he whose matted locks are the tangled hair of <s>Śiva</s> be for your victory —
he in whom even the <s>Ganges</s>, settling at the topknot, creates the illusion of a single grey hair!
May he protect you, in the chaplet of whose matted locks
rests the moon, bright as a glistening pearl necklace,
like a swan sleeping among a cluster of blue-lotus stalks
in the autumn!
May he whose ornament is the cool-rayed [moon] grant you welfare —
he upon whose brow the celestial river,
with undulating waves like wings, like a female swan
seeking the lotus-root of the stainless crescent-moon, fell from the sky!
May he bestow blessings upon you, on whose crest the supreme garland
of the heavenly river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>) shines bright as a white cloud —
like an ambrosia-bearing stream of the melting
moon-nectar, dissolving in the heat of the upward-gazing [third] eye's blaze!
Slowly reuniting the crescent slipped from the moon with the bracelet broken in the quarrel of love,
the mountain's daughter (<s>Pārvatī</s>), with a laughing face,

children.text: avocadyaṃ paśyotyavatu sa śivaḥ sā ca girijā
children.translated_text: said 'Look!' — may that <s>Śiva</s> and that <s>Girijā</s> protect you,
along with that playful moon, its body filled with the rays of [her] teeth!

children.text: eṣā te hara kā sugātri katamā mūrdhni sthitā kiṃ jaṭā
children.translated_text: 'This one on your head, O <s>Hara</s> — who is she, O beautiful one?' 'Which one?' 'The one standing on your head.' 'You mean a matted lock?'

children.text: haṃsaḥ kiṃ bhajate jaṭāṃ nahi śaśī candro jalaṃ sevate /
children.translated_text: 'Does a swan dwell in matted hair? No — it's the moon.' 'Does the moon serve water?'
'Fool, this is sacred ash.' 'Whence water here?' 'Sacred ash billows like waves!'

children.text: evaṃ yo vinigūhate tripathagāṃ pāyātsa vaḥ śaṃkaraḥ //
children.translated_text: May <s>Śaṅkara</s>, who thus conceals the triple-pathed river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), protect you!
'Let embraces, lip-kissing, loving words, and smiles remain

children.text: dūre tāvadidaṃ mitho na sulabhaṃ jātaṃ mukhālokanam /
children.translated_text: far off for now — even this mutual beholding of faces is not easily obtained.'
Thus, for us two whose attempt at becoming one body has been rendered fruitless,
what mockery of love is this? — may the smiling <s>Ardhanārīśvara</s> (half-woman Lord) protect you!
'Mother, what is this that father guards in his cupped palms?' — 'Dear child, it is a sweet fruit.' — 'He won't give it to me!' — 'Go and take it yourself.'

children.text: vatsa svādu phalaṃ prayacchati na me gatvā gṛhāṇa svayam /

children.translated_text: When the mother thus sent him home, and he pulled apart [<s>Śiva</s>'s] twilight-prayer <s>añjali</s> (folded hands),
may the burst of laughter from <s>Śambhu</s>, whose meditation was broken and whose composure was checked, protect you!
One of [his] eyelids flutters from the muttering of <s>japa</s> (prayer); the other half [opens] from anger;

children.text: ekaḥ pāṇiḥ praṇantuṃ śirasi kṛtapadaḥ kṣeptumanyastameva /
children.translated_text: one hand is placed on [his] head to bow, the other to throw that very [hand off];
one eye closes in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), the other cannot bear to look — thus,

children.text: tulyānicchāpi vāmā tanuravatu sa vo yasya saṃdhyāvasāne //
children.translated_text: may the left half of his body — equally unwilling, yet female — protect you at the end of twilight prayer!
Of that household occupied with the feeding at the breast of the son of the Mountain-King's daughter,
may the remaining crooked lotuses — deprived of milk-drinking — remove your impurities!
May the unprecedented play of the ray-hands of the fiery one (the Sun), which grants all desires, be [auspicious] for you —
by whose worship, liberation from the bondage of existence is accomplished for those who bow down.
May the first rays of the jewel of the sky (the Sun), which bear the blush of sunrise,
bring you auspiciousness —
they who, at the grand festival of the birth of day,
make the guardian goddesses of the directions look like women with sindūra-reddened faces!
With radiance rising from the arm's disc, with armored chest,
warm, wounded, maddening to the hearts of adversaries, rough,
their full forms visible when garments are cast aside — his warriors in the vanguard of Love,

children.text: yodhā vāravadhūstanāśca na dadhuḥ kṣobhaṃ sa vovyājjinaḥ //
children.translated_text: and the breasts of courtesans too — could not disturb him. May that Victor (<s>Jina</s>) protect you!
'Is it the sun? No, the sun's feet do not drip with dense nectar-juice.

children.text: kiṃ vā rākāśaśāṅko nahi tuhinaruciḥ kutracinniṣkalaṅkaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or the full moon? No, the cool-rayed one is nowhere without blemish.
The <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) itself? Whence such delicacy in a large-fruited gem?' —

children.text: saṃdehānmugdhadhībhiḥ prathamamiti muneḥ pātu dṛṣṭaṃ vapurvaḥ //
children.translated_text: May the form of the sage, first seen thus with doubt by those of simple minds, protect you!
May the bow-drawings of <s>Caṇḍī</s> (<s>Durgā</s>), which long manifested joy and fear in enemies,
mingled with the twang of the bowstring, protect you!
May the pair of lotus-feet of <s>Caṇḍī</s> bestow upon you the desired [blessings],
with rays of nails like lotus-stalks swaying over the lake-like heads of great <s>asuras</s>,
with dancing and restless ankle-bells
whose humming rivals that of bees!
Bashful upon the beloved's face; compassionate upon the elephant-hide garment;
fearful upon the serpent; filled with wonder at the moon dripping nectar;
jealous upon seeing the daughter of <s>Jahnu</s> (<s>Gaṅgā</s>); sorrowful upon the skull-bowl —
may <s>Pārvatī</s>'s glance, tender with the love of a new union, bring you welfare!
Rising at the end of lovemaking, placing the heavy serpent-king on one hand,
holding her garment with the other, bearing on her shoulder the loosened mass of hair —
when <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), whose delight in love was doubled by her beauty at that moment,
drew her back to the bed in an embrace — may that form of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, with languidly moving arms, purify you!
May the Elephant-faced one (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) protect these three worlds —
he by whose great trunk, raised into the sky,
with a white tusk-sprout clinging at the root,
the disc of the sun appeared stalked like a lotus!
As <s>Nandī</s> joyfully beats the drum, and the <s>Kaumāra</s> (son of <s>Kumāra</s>) peacock,
frightened by the sound, enters the nostril-hole of the serpent-lord who contracts his coils,
while the directions resound with the buzzing bee-garlands flying from his cheeks, during the <s>Tāṇḍava</s> dance of the Trident-bearer —
may the exhalations of <s>Gaṇeśa</s>'s (<s>Vināyaka</s>'s) mouth, accompanied by hissing sounds, protect you long!
His bow is a garland of flowers, his bowstring the humming row of bees, his target is a woman,

children.text: mano bhedyaṃ śabdaprabhṛtaya ime pañca viśikhāḥ /
children.translated_text: the mind is what must be pierced; sound and the other [senses] are his five arrows.
Such is the power of him who conquers the three worlds without a body —
may that <s>Kāma</s> (god of Love), dwelling in the sidelong glance of his beloved, grant you your desires!
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, Wind, Fire, Moon, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>,
mountains, rivers, oceans, planetary hosts, humans, <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>,
islands, stars, constellations, Sun, <s>Vasus</s>, sages, sky, earth, and the two twilights —

children.text: saṃlīnā yasya sarve vapuṣi sa bhagavāpātu vo viśvarūpaḥ //
children.translated_text: all merged in whose body — may that Lord, the Cosmic Form (<s>Viśvarūpa</s>), protect you!
'O innocent one, abandon your sorrow! The trembling of <s>Indra</s>'s slayer (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) is serious — let it go.
Be sincere, O lotus-eyed one! Respect those who deserve respect.'
While <s>Dhanvantari</s> was instructing <s>Lakṣmī</s> at her own <s>svayaṃvara</s> (self-choice ceremony) — by a slip of tongue,

children.text: danyatra pratiṣedhamātmani vidhiṃ śṛṇvanhariḥ pātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: [saying] 'prohibition elsewhere, but permission for yourself' — may <s>Hari</s>, hearing this, protect you!
May <s>Narahari</s> (the Man-Lion), the sole hero of the universe, grant you happiness —
he who, when rising to tear apart the son of <s>Diti</s> in battle,
displayed such a wrathful face that even the inability
to look at it became apparent even on his own nails!

children.text: svasti svāgatamarthyahaṃ vada vibho kiṃ dīyatāṃ medinī
children.translated_text: 'Welcome! Greetings! I am the suppliant — speak, O Lord!' 'What shall be given?' 'The earth!' 'What measure?' 'The span of three steps.' 'Granted — I have taken it.'

children.text: kā mātrā mama vikramatrayapadaṃ dattaṃ gṛhītāṃ mayā /
mā dehītyuśanāḥ kuto harirayaṃ pātraṃ kimasmātparaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Don't give!' [cried] <s>Uśanas</s> (<s>Śukra</s>). 'Why? This is <s>Hari</s>!' 'What better recipient than he?'

children.text: yo hītthaṃ balinārcito makhamukhe pāyātsa vo vāmanaḥ //
children.translated_text: He who was thus worshipped by <s>Bali</s> at the head of the sacrifice — may that <s>Vāmana</s> protect you!

children.text: cakra brūhi vibho gade jaya hare kambo samājñāpaya
children.translated_text: 'O discus, speak! Victory, O Lord! O mace, hail, O <s>Hari</s>! O conch, command!

children.text: bho bho nandaka jīva pannagariyo kiṃ nātha bhinno mayā /
children.translated_text: Ho, <s>Nandaka</s> (sword), rejoice! O serpent-enemy — what, my Lord? Am I cleft by you?'

children.text: ko daityaḥ katamo hiraṇyakaśipuḥ satyaṃ bhavadbhyaḥ śape
children.translated_text: 'What <s>Daitya</s>?' 'Which <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>!' 'Truly? I swear to you!' 'With what weapon?' 'With nails!' —

children.text: kenāstreṇa nakhairiti pravadato viṣṇormukhaṃ pātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: may the face of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, speaking thus [to his own weapons], protect you!
When the discus-bearer was full of anxiety, the lotus-seated one (<s>Brahmā</s>) in fear,
the blazing one (Sun) losing his radiance, the moon firmly seized with doubt,

children.text: bhraśyaccetasi ca pracetasi śucā tānte kṛtānte ca yo
children.translated_text: the mind of the Ocean-lord failing, and Death (<s>Yama</s>) himself grieving —
he who eagerly [stepped forth] to swallow the terrible <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison — may that one protect you!
The ever-returning supreme <s>Brahman</s>, whose sole measure is the experience of one's own Self,
the abode of bliss, the one seed from which the world sprouts,
intolerable to the crushing hands of direction, place, time, and all the rest —
may that great radiance grant you happiness!
Like the mass of rain-clouds in the sky, like the array of waves
in a lake, like the glow of the thousand-rayed moon —
in whom this world arises and dissolves —
may that <s>Śāmbhava</s> (glory of <s>Śiva</s>) bring you prosperity!
He who, for the sport of creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the three worlds,
assumes by function the nature of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> —
may that god, whose power transcends the speech and mind of all beings,
grant you perpetual, imperishable welfare!
This entire helpless aggregate — the subtle soul, <s>karma</s>,
body, and other instrumental groups — by whose grace
the universe attains the skill of manifold creation —
may that one great Lord of the three worlds protect you!
He who, as if with balls, plays with <s>Indra</s>, the lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>),
the lord of <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), and others — that unfathomable, insurmountable Lord,
the beloved of the <s>Himālaya</s>'s daughter, the crusher of Death —
may he lighten your burdens!
<s>Mukti</s> (liberation) is indeed the single, supreme goal of human life;
those who know the inner [truth] consider it the [only true] obstacle-free [goal].
What need of more? May your unbreakable devotion
to him whose crest-jewel is the crescent of the moon of nectar be [your liberation]!
The form of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), adorned once with <s>Kṛttikā</s>, ever with <s>Rohiṇī</s>,
eldest with <s>Bhadrapadā</s>, joined with <s>Punarvasu</s>, beautiful with <s>Citrā</s>, accompanied by <s>Viśākhā</s>,
victorious with <s>Āṣāḍhā</s> grasped at the root of the hand, adorned with <s>Maghā</s>,
accompanied by <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (<s>Kubera</s>) — may the constellation-garland of the Lord bestow welfare upon you!

children.text: trātā bhītibhṛtāṃ patiścidacitāṃ kleśaṃ sataṃ śaṃsatāṃ
children.translated_text: Protector of the frightened, lord of the sentient and insentient, declaring the grief of the good,
destroyer [of sins] of the devoted, equalizer of the good, undoer of the wicked —
the god whose play manifests the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of his servants' enjoyment and liberation, the three worlds, and the triple Veda —
may <s>Mṛḍa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) protect you!
The king whose feet are worshipped by kings; the digit of whose [moon] never wanes, being a crest-jewel;
the <s>Nāgas</s> who ornament [him] are not [merely] white with ash, but [glow with] <s>Gaurī</s>'s (<s>Pārvatī</s>'s) half-body;

children.text: mā rāmārāgiṇī bhūnmatiriti yamināṃ yena vodāhi māraḥ
children.translated_text: 'May the mind not become enamored of <s>Rāma</s>!' — thus <s>Kāma</s> was dispatched by him for the <s>yogis</s> —
may the seven-horsed one (<s>Sūrya</s>, or rather <s>Śiva</s>), bearing three eyes, whose rays are like the dawn, protect you!
As [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] was about to go from <s>Candrāvalī</s>'s house to the temple of <s>Rādhā</s>'s enchantment,

children.text: rādho kṣemamiti priyasya vacanaṃ śrutvāha candrāvalī /
children.translated_text: hearing the beloved's words 'Is <s>Rādhā</s> well?' — <s>Candrāvalī</s> replied:

children.text: kṣemaṃ kaṃsa tataḥ priyaḥ prakupitaḥ kaṃsaḥ kva dṛṣṭastvayā
children.translated_text: '<s>Kaṃsa</s> is well.' Then the beloved, angered: 'Where did you see <s>Kaṃsa</s>?' 'Where is <s>Rādhā</s>?'

children.text: rādhā kveti tayoḥ prisannamanasorhāsodgamaḥ pātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: May the burst of laughter of those two, their minds now pleased, protect you!

children.text: ākṛṣṭe yudhi kārmuke samavadadvāmaḥ karo dakṣiṇaṃ
children.translated_text: When the bow was drawn in battle, the left hand said to the right:

children.text: re re dakṣiṇahasta bhojanamahādānādi te kurvataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Hey, right hand! While you are busy with great gifts of food and such,
it is not proper for you to go behind [me]!' Then the other replied: 'Let me go swiftly
to ask <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>): shall I split the heads of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>?'

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ kvāpi sa keśavo vrajavadhūmādāya kāṃcidgataḥ
children.translated_text: '<s>Keśava</s> has been seen somewhere; he has gone off with some <s>Vraja</s> woman!

children.text: sarvā eva hi vañcitāḥ khula vayaṃ sonveṣaṇīyo yadi /
children.translated_text: All of us have been deceived! He should be searched for —

children.text: dve dve gacchata ityudīrya sahasā rādhāṃ gṛhītvā kare
children.translated_text: go two by two!' — having said this, suddenly taking <s>Rādhā</s> by the hand,

children.text: gopīveṣadharo nikuñjabhavanaṃ prāpto hariḥ pātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: may <s>Hari</s>, disguised as a <s>gopī</s>, who entered the bower-house, protect you!
'Mother, I will not go to the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> to guard the calves!'
'Why, child?' 'The <s>gopī</s> women crush me with their heavy pair of breasts!'
Though checked many times with frowning brows, while he prattled on before <s>Yaśodā</s>,
may that <s>Keśava</s>, whose mouth was covered by the lotus-hands of the <s>gopīs</s>, protect you!
'That you bow to the twilight before everyone with folded hands, I will endure;

children.text: dhatse yacca nadīṃ vilajja śirasā tannāma soḍhaṃ mayā /
children.translated_text: that you bear the river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>) shamelessly upon your head — even that name I have tolerated.',
'If <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) went to <s>Hari</s> at the churning of nectar, why did you eat the poison?'

children.text: mā strīlaṃpaṭa māṃ spṛśeti gadito gauryā haraḥ pātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Don't touch me, you philanderer!' — thus scolded by <s>Gaurī</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), may <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) protect you!

children.text: kastvaṃ śūlī mṛgaya bhiṣajaṃ nīlakaṇṭhaḥ priyehaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Who are you?' 'The Trident-bearer.' 'Seek a physician.' 'I am <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> (Blue-throated).' 'My dear!'
'Utter just one cry!' 'But <s>Paśupati</s> (Lord of beasts), no horn is visible!'

children.text: mugdhe sthāṇuḥ sa carati kathaṃ jīviteśaḥ śivāyā
children.translated_text: 'Innocent one, that is a stump!' 'Then how does he move?' 'He is the lord of <s>Śivā</s>'s (Pārvatī's) life!'
May <s>Candracūḍa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), rendered speechless thus [by <s>Pārvatī</s>] with 'Go to the forest!', protect you!

children.text: koyaṃ dvāri hariḥ prayāhyupavanaḥ śākhāmṛgasyātra kiṃ
children.translated_text: 'Who is at the door?' '<s>Hari</s>.' 'Go away to the garden.' 'What [business have you] with the monkey?'

children.text: kṛṣṇohaṃ dayite bibhemi sutarāṃ kṛṣṇādahaṃ vānarāt /
children.translated_text: 'I am <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O beloved!' 'I am even more afraid — of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' 'I [mean] the monkey?!'

children.text: mugdhehaṃ madhusūdanaḥ piba latāṃ tāmeva tanmīvale
children.translated_text: 'Innocent one, I am <s>Madhusūdana</s> (slayer of the demon Madhu)!' 'Then drink that very creeper [of wine]!' 'That [bee-swarm] is...'

children.text: itthaṃ nirvacanīkṛto dayitayā hrīto hariḥ pātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: May <s>Hari</s>, thus rendered speechless by his beloved and [then] embraced, protect you!

children.text: nirlajja hare kimidaṃ pramadānugataḥ sadā paribhramasi /
children.translated_text: 'Shameless <s>Hari</s>! What is this — you wander always in the company of women!'
'Innocent one, from your company I become delighted (<s>pramada</s>) — what is wonderful in that?'
'O deceitful one, I shall describe — the love of women for you is excessive!'
'What nonsense do you prattle? Who has love for enemies (<s>ari</s>)?'
'Why do you thus delude? I speak of your attachment to <s>Rāma</s> (women/Lakṣmī)!'

children.text: jyeṣṭhe bhrātari rāme na kriyatāṃ kathamivāsaktiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'As for <s>Rāma</s>, the elder brother — how can attachment to him be improper?'

children.text: kiṃ māmevaṃ bhramayasi śocāmi vyasanameva bhavadīyam /
children.translated_text: 'Why do you thus confuse me? I grieve for your very misfortune (<s>vyasana</s>)!'
'When you are angry without cause, tell me, what misfortune is small?'
Having thus silenced the <s>gopī</s> with such crooked words,
may the tight embrace of <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), [given to her] with her rounded heavy breasts pressed close, protect you!

children.text: ayi saṃprasīda pārvati śivopi tava pādayornipatitoham /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Pārvatī</s>, please be gracious! Even <s>Śiva</s> has fallen at your feet — I!'

children.text: śiva iti kathaṃ hi jalpasi sarudhiragajacarmasaṃvītaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'How can you speak of "<s>Śiva</s>" (auspicious), clad as you are in a blood-stained elephant-skin?'

children.text: śiva iti yadi tava gadite dviguṇo roṣo bhavāmyahaṃ sthāṇuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If at your saying "<s>Śiva</s>" my anger is doubled, I am [indeed] a <s>sthāṇu</s> (pillar/stump)!'
'You are a <s>sthāṇu</s> (post) indeed — this is true! In your heart there is nothing at all!'
'O proud one, abandon anger! Know me as the Lord, worshipped by the three worlds!'
'O <s>Tryambaka</s> (three-eyed one), if you are the Lord, why [are you] naked and smeared with dust?'
'What will you say now? I am <s>Paśupati</s> (lord of creatures), O white-cheeked one!'
'You are indeed <s>Paśupati</s> (lord of beasts) — that is why you do not consider what is proper or improper!'

children.text: mugdhe bhramasi kimevaṃ satyamimaṃ māṃ bhavaṃ vijānīhi /
children.translated_text: 'Innocent one, why do you err thus? Truly, know me as <s>Bhava</s> (existence/Śiva)!'
'Truly you are <s>Bhava</s> (worldly existence), O rogue — that is why your form is so strange!'

children.text: paṇḍitabādastava yadi lokehaṃ tryambako vidita eṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Your argument is powerful — if in the world I am known as <s>Tryambaka</s> (three-eyed/three-mothered)!'

children.text: ambā hyekāpi na te prajalpasi tvaṃ kutastisraḥ //
children.translated_text: 'But you have not even one <s>ambā</s> (mother)! You prattle — how then three?'

children.text: vādo mahānihaiva hi tathā vijānīhyanaṅgadahanaṃ mām /
children.translated_text: 'This very argument is the great one! Then know me as the burner of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless one, Kāma)!'
'This body of mine has been burned (<s>dagdha</s>), limb by limb, by your very deeds of this kind!'
When he, defeated by <s>Pārvatī</s>, appeases her for the fault of [late] evening salutation,

children.text: āliṅgitaśca sarabhasamurasā vai haratu duritaṃ vaḥ //
children.translated_text: and is hastily embraced by her to his chest — may he remove your sins!

children.text: bhava niḥsnehastvaṃ me na bhavāmyevaṃ yathā tvayā gaditam /
children.translated_text: 'You are devoid of affection (<s>sneha</s>) toward me, O <s>Bhava</s>!' 'I am not as you say.'
'O Goddess, whence has arisen this desire for [my] lack of affection (<s>niḥsnehatā</s> / ununctuousness)?'
'Enough of these wicked tricks! For what purpose is this river (<s>nadī</s>) upon you?'
'What? It is a garland of human skulls upon me — take these!'
'Thus you torment a person who loves you, by [such] false behavior!'
'[It is] with your rows of human skulls that one must necessarily stand above!'

children.text: kiṃ kupitosi tyaja ruṣamapanayatāṃ vigrahaṃ mayā hi bhavān /
children.translated_text: 'Why are you angry? Abandon wrath — let the quarrel be ended by me, for you —'

children.text: saha vigraho bhavatyā na jātu vighāṭiṣyatesmākam //
children.translated_text: '[My] quarrel with you shall never be dissolved!'
Having thus teased <s>Gaurī</s> into speechlessness with words [punning on the] <s>Gaṅgā</s> quarrel, may <s>Śiva</s>, who then appeased her, bring you well-being!

children.text: parihāsya yonuninye sa karotu śivaḥ śivaṃ bhavatām //
children.translated_text: [Empty segment — continuation of above verse]

children.text: vijaye kuśalastryakṣo na krīḍitumahamanena saha śaktā /
children.translated_text: 'The three-eyed one is skilled at dice (<s>vijaya</s>)!' 'I am not able to play with him.'

children.text: vijaye kuśalosmi na tu tryakṣokṣadvayamidaṃ pāṇau //
children.translated_text: 'I am skilled at dice — but the three-eyed one? These are two dice (<s>akṣa</s>/eyes) in my hand!'

children.text: kiṃ me durodareṇa prayātu yadi gaṇapatirna tebhimataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What use to me is this one with the big belly?' 'Go away, if <s>Gaṇapati</s> is not to your liking!'

children.text: kaḥ pradveṣṭi vināyakamahilokaḥ kiṃ na jānāsi //
children.translated_text: 'Who hates <s>Vināyaka</s> (the remover of obstacles)? Does the whole world not know this?'

children.text: vasurahitena krīḍā bhavatā saha kīdṛśī na jihreṣi /
children.translated_text: 'What kind of play is it with you, who are without wealth (<s>vasu</s>)? Are you not ashamed?'
'Why without <s>Vasu</s>? Look before you — the gods and demons [who are] different from <s>Vasu</s>!'

children.text: candragrahaṇena vinā nāsmi rame kiṃ pravartayasyevam /
children.translated_text: 'Without the eclipse of the moon, I find no pleasure! Why do you insist thus?'
'If this pleases the Goddess, O <s>Nandin</s>, let <s>Rāhu</s> be summoned!'

children.text: hā rāhau nikaṭasthe sitadaṃṣṭre bhayakṛti ratiḥ kasya /
children.translated_text: 'Alas! When <s>Rāhu</s>, of white fangs and terrifying, is near — who can feel pleasure?'
'If you do not wish it, then this serpent-necklace is hereby discarded!'
'Do you ascribe [things] to me in vain? Am I not familiar with your lap?'
'After sitting for a divine thousand years, it is proper to speak thus!'
Thus, may the face of <s>Bhavānī</s> — with pupils trembling with joy
at the playfully crooked words deployed through the charming noose-play of <s>Paśupati</s> — open [in a smile] for you!

children.text: aṅgulyā kaḥ kavāṭe praharati kuṭilo mādhavaḥ kiṃ vasanto
children.translated_text: 'Who knocks at the door with a finger?' 'The crooked <s>Mādhava</s>.' 'Is it the spring?'

children.text: no cakrī kiṃ kulālo nahi dharaṇidharaḥ kiṃ praṇīndro dvijihvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'No, the disc-bearer.' 'A potter?' 'No, the mountain-holder.' 'A great serpent?' 'The forked-tongued one?'

children.text: mugdhe ghorāhimāthī kimuta khagapatirno hariḥ kiṃ kapīndra
children.translated_text: 'Innocent one, the terrible serpent-churner!' 'Then the lord of birds?' 'No, <s>Hari</s>!' 'Then the king of monkeys?'

children.text: itthaṃ lakṣmyā kṛtosau pratihatavacanaḥ pātulakṣmīdhavo vaḥ //
children.translated_text: May the Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, thus rendered speechless by <s>Lakṣmī</s>, protect you!

children.text: khedaḥ kiṃ khalu dayite na vetsi ravimaṇḍalaṃ jagadviditam /
children.translated_text: 'What sorrow? O beloved, do you not know the orb of the sun, known to all the world?'

children.text: na krodhaḥ kartavyo jalacaramūrdhvaṃ na jātu paśyāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'No anger should be shown — the water-creature [fish] we never see above!'

children.text: kopastyaktuṃ yogyo yasya pipāsā na saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: 'Anger should be abandoned by one in whom thirst does not arise!'

children.text: saṃtyaja mānini mānaṃ kiṃ mānenādhunā mamānena //
children.translated_text: 'O proud one, abandon pride — what use is pride to me, this wretch?'

children.text: kiṃ tena kila kāvyena mṛdyamānasya yasya tāḥ /
children.translated_text: What use is that poetry from which, when it is being pressed,
streams of the nectar of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic delight) do not flow, as from the ocean?

children.text: kiṃ kavestasya kāvyena kiṃ kāṇḍena dhanuṣmataḥ /
children.translated_text: What use is the poetry of that poet, what use is the shaft of the archer,

children.text: parasya hṛdaye lagnaṃ na ghūrṇayati yacchiraḥ //
children.translated_text: which, lodged in another's heart, does not make the head spin?
There are some poets, like children — with faltering arrangement of words,
causing maternal affection, and babbling much.
What use is that honey of poetry, flooded with streams of <s>rasa</s>,
by which even dull-minded persons do not sprout the horripilation [of aesthetic response]?
Novel meaning, non-rustic diction, unstrained <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), manifest <s>rasa</s>,
and absence of harsh word-arrangement — all this together in one [poem] is difficult.
An insensitive person appreciates poetry by its face [surface] alone,
as <s>Rāhu</s> [mistakes] even the shadow of [the real] dark beauty for the lord of stars (the moon).
The connoisseurs are seized by envy, the wealthy are tainted by arrogance,
and the rest are afflicted by ignorance — good poetry (<s>subhāṣita</s>) grows old upon one's body.
Villains, unable even to compose two lines,
are nevertheless unperturbed [in criticizing] even difficult compositions of others.

children.text: kva doṣotra mayā labhya iti saṃcintya cetasā /
children.translated_text: 'Where can I find a fault here?' — pondering thus in his mind,
the villain applies himself to listening to the poems of the virtuous.
Unfading through [logical] proofs, not diminished by didacticism,
having an essence knowable through self-experience — such are the utterances of the sympathetic critic (<s>sahṛdaya</s>).
In the mouths of some, [good sayings are] like a parrot; in the hearts of others, like a mute;
but for a rare few, fine sayings leap beautifully from heart to mouth.
Many are the human heads — hairy and large —
fastened upon necks; but among them, few are those with ears [that can hear].
Like a virtuous wife, the speech (<s>Bhāratī</s>) of the great poet shines —
devoted to the vow of good expression, untouched by vulgar subject matter.

children.text: te vandyāste mahātmānasteṣāṃ loke sthiraṃ yaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Worthy of homage are those great souls; their fame in the world is lasting —

children.text: yairnibaddhāni kāvyānī ye vā kāvyeṣu kīrtitāḥ //
children.translated_text: those by whom poems are composed, and those who are celebrated in poems.
Clear, captivating in beauty, skilled in various modes of <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) —
by someone's merit, such [qualities appear]: in the mouth, words; in the home, women.
By the well-chosen sayings of great poets — which pierce with concealed deeper meanings —
how can there be no pain for the listener whose knowledge is being pierced?

children.text: yāsyati sajjanahastaṃ ramayiṣyati taṃ bhavecca nirdoṣā /
children.translated_text: 'It will reach the hands of the good, it will delight him, and it will be flawless' —
even after producing [such a work], the poet labors over the narrative, as over a daughter.
Everything recited at the right moment attains the quality of a <s>subhāṣita</s> (fine saying);

children.text: kṣudhi kadaśanamapi nitarāṃ bhoktuḥ saṃpadyate svādu //
children.translated_text: in hunger, even a poor meal becomes exceedingly delicious to the eater.
Poetry-gold, heated by the fire of the wicked, attains purification;
therefore, it should be deliberately shown to those of envious minds.

children.text: gaṇayanti nāpaśabdaṃ na vṛttabhaṅgaṃ kṣatiṃ na cārthasya /
children.translated_text: They do not count wrong words, nor broken metres, nor loss of meaning —
agitated by their connoisseurship: patrons of courtesans and bad poets.

children.text: vipulahṛdayābhiyogye khidyati kāvye jaḍo na maurkhye sve /
children.translated_text: The dull person is vexed by a poem worthy of a capacious heart, not by his own stupidity;
usually, a woman with withered breasts blames the bodice itself.

children.text: khyātiṃ gamayati sujanaḥ sukavirvidadhāti kevalaṃ kāvyam /
children.translated_text: The good person gives fame; the skilled poet merely creates the poem;
water nourishes the lotus, but it is the sun that endows it with <s>Lakṣmī</s> (beauty).
Some are skilled only in expounding scripture, while others are capable of applying it;
the hand brings food close, but only the tongue knows the flavors.

children.text: jivita iva kaṇṭhagate sūkte duḥkhāsikā kavestāvat /
children.translated_text: When a fine saying (<s>sūkti</s>) is lodged in the throat as if at the throat of life, the poet feels a sword-like pain,
until there arrives the conscious one [a sympathetic listener] who causes the blossoming of the eyes.
What appears to be apprehended is actually something else entirely —
such is the substance in the compositions of great poets;
that which shines beyond the well-known parts
is like <s>lāvaṇya</s> (gracefulness) in women.
The poet's intention, beyond the reach of words,
flashing only in the tender phrases,
speaking through limbs [of the body] transformed with horripilation —
this is the silent homage of the audience.
Those few sympathetic listeners (<s>sahṛdayas</s>) among the poet's compositions —
these are not the unrestrained ones;
like bees on rasa-filled creepers,
they savor the heart's essence, not merely the surface.
Kings become famous through the patronage of poets,
and poets attain renown through the patronage of kings;
there is no greater benefactor of the king than the poet,

children.text: rājño na cāsti kavinā sadṛśaḥ sahāyaḥ //
children.translated_text: nor is there a companion equal to the poet for the king.
Generating clarity of mind in the noblest of the wise,
joyous, endowed with all <s>rasas</s>, exceedingly lucid —

children.text: kāvyaṃ khalasya na karoti hṛdi pratiṣṭhāṃ
children.translated_text: poetry does not find a place in the heart of the villain,
like the drinking of ambrosia in the open mouth of <s>Rāhu</s>.
Bound by the delight of the mirror [of poetry], through the process of rubbing —
how could they not instantly yield their original meanings?
Like exceedingly gentle thieves, the words of great poets
forcefully deliver even unintended meanings (<s>arthāntara</s>).
What kind of poetry is it that, like drinking abundant wine, does not produce, upon entering the heart,
even in those whose minds are veiled by envy, the involuntary rising of the hair by the power of <s>rasa</s>,
trembling of the head, a flush on both cheeks, eyes brimming with tears,
speech engaged in celebrating imagined [poetic] objects, and the grasping of hands [in wonder]?
Those who are nourished by their own virtues — for them the world is a wilderness;

children.text: yepyete kṛtamatsarāḥ paraguṇaṃ svapnepi necchanti te /
children.translated_text: those who are given to envy do not desire the virtue of another even in a dream;
of the rest, who are affectionate — some have tender hearts, filled with delight —

children.text: vitthaṃ yāntu tapovanāni mahatāṃ sūktāni manyedhunā //
children.translated_text: thus, I think, the fine sayings of the great now depart for the hermitages.
That vision which does not make even those who are silent through envy

children.text: proccairno kurute satāṃ matimatāṃ dṛṣṭirna sā vāstavī /
children.translated_text: cry out 'Well said!' as if [praising] the virtuous — that vision is not authentic;

children.text: yā yātāḥ śrutigocaraṃ ca sahasā harṣollasatkaṃdharās-
children.translated_text: for even animals, upon hearing [poetry], their necks suddenly thrilled with joy,

children.text: tiryañcopi na muktaśaṣpakavalāstāḥ kiṃ kavīnāṃ giraḥ //
children.translated_text: do not release the mouthful of grass — are those then the words of poets?
Riches cannot be held back — like lightning in a cloud of capricious fortune;
the faith in the travel-drum of the life-breath never rests;

children.text: trāṇaṃ yetra yaśomaye vapuṣi vaḥ kurvanti kāvyāmṛtais-
children.translated_text: those [poets] who provide protection through the ambrosia of poetry in your fame-body —
place those good poets in a worshipful position, O kings, without arrogance!
O kings, abandon hostility in the bond of love with good poets!
Your pure fame surely shines by their grace;
when pleased, they composed the noble character of the lord of the <s>Raghus</s>;
when displeased, they led the conqueror of the three worlds (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) along the path of ridicule.
Salutations, salutations to that essence of poetic <s>rasa</s>,
even a drop of which, sprinkled within,
makes the face of the good person turn golden,
and that of the wicked turn dark!
Those who, unaware of the secret seal of true learning,
hold conceit on the path of poetry —
they, without having studied the <s>Gāruḍī</s> (anti-venom) mantras,
begin to taste the <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison).
He who for long did not suckle the breast of Mother <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
dense [with the milk] of poetic skill and learning —
how can he, whose every limb has not obtained proper development,
attain special maturity day by day?
Like royal swans that are the vehicles of <s>Sarasvatī</s>
stationed in the heart, having bestowed instruction —
those who are skilled in discriminating milk from water —
Victorious are those poets who possess discernment! //
The nectar of poetry, eclipsed by the <s>Rāhu</s> of the wicked,
would not be attainable by good-minded people,
were it not for the sharpness that shines forth genuinely
from the true process, without pretense. //
Without one skilled in literature, the virtues of poets
cannot spread in any way in this world.
A drop of oil spreads its expanse
only in water at that very moment, not elsewhere. //
That [speech] which is excessively crooked is meaningless,
and which, devoid of all other qualities, reveals [only crookedness] —
what use is that speech, tainted by untouchability,
like the tuft of a worthless dog's tail? //
Let the lowly one shed tears, let the deep blackness
be nourished by collyrium, which shares its nature.
But how can the clarity of <s>Sarasvatī</s>'s (the goddess of learning) eye
arise from that one's worthless powder? //
If there is meaning but no purity of words; if that too exists,

children.text: no rītirasti yadi sā ghaṭanā kutastyā /
children.translated_text: but no style; if style exists, but the composition is lacking;
if that too exists, but no novel and striking expression — then
all is in vain without <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). Ah, how deep is the art of poetry! //
Praiseworthy indeed is the curved path of the creeper-bow
of the fine sayings of the best poets, bound firmly like a dense [bowstring].
When its quality, which wins the affection of the ear,
[is heard,] the hearts of the envious instantly shatter. //
Those few who formerly, pressing and pressing the sugarcane-stalk of the essence of speech,
extracted the method of gathering the essence of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), touching the truth —

children.text: jāyantedya yathāyathaṃ tu kavayaste tatra saṃtanvate
children.translated_text: the poets born today, in their own ways, pile up there
a heap of thorns — harsh <s>prāsa</s> (rhyme), obscure <s>citra</s> (pictorial verse), <s>yamaka</s> (alliterative play), <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) and the like. //
Those who daily practice a few verses of others

children.text: catuṣpādīṃ kuryurbahava iha te santi kavayaḥ /
children.translated_text: and then compose a four-lined [stanza] — many such poets exist here.
But the words of certain [poets] — friendly with the style [that flows like] unbroken, rising waves of the ocean,

children.text: suhṛdyā vaiśadyaṃ dadhati kila keṣāmcana giraḥ //
children.translated_text: delightful — possess a clarity indeed. //

children.text: hemno bhāraśatāni vā madamucāṃ vṛndāni vā dantināṃ
children.translated_text: Hundreds of measures of gold, or herds of rut-dripping elephants —

children.text: śrīharṣeṇa samarpitāni guṇine bāṇāya kutrādya tat /
children.translated_text: these were offered by <s>Śrīharṣa</s> to the meritorious <s>Bāṇa</s>. Where is all that today?

children.text: yā bāṇena tu tasya sūktivisarairuṭṭaṅkitāḥ kīrtayas-
children.translated_text: But the fames engraved by <s>Bāṇa</s> with his showers of fine sayings —

children.text: tāḥ kalpapralayepi yānti na manāṅmanye parimlānatām //
children.translated_text: even at the dissolution of a world-age, those do not in the least fade, I believe. //
Blessed are the flowers of good sayings, plucked from
the creeper of speech growing in the garden of one's own mouth —
pure, fragrant, rich in virtues,
of select colors — which [the virtuous] make ear-ornaments on the shores of the ear! //
Therefore, like voyagers who have seen the far shore of the great ocean of all literature,
the great poets are victorious.
With clove, lavender, and the finest [spices] of their good sayings,
the virtuous perfume the assemblies with the fragrance of beautiful speech. //
The jewel-ornament of the three worlds, the kinsman of the community of the meritorious —
the poet alone shines, a second sun of poetry.
Whose surpassing greatness even the mountains proclaim,
bowing their heads and grasping his feet. //
Even those who do not understand the mere meaning of words,
drinking through their ears, like deer [entranced] by music,
become arrested in all their faculties,
as if fixed in a painting — we bow to that speech of the king of poets! //

children.text: asthāne gamitā layaṃ hatadhiyāṃ vāgdevatā kalpate
children.translated_text: The goddess of speech, brought to dissolution in the wrong place by the dull-witted,

children.text: dhikkārāya parābhavāya mahate tāpāya pāpāya vā /
children.translated_text: serves for reproach, for great humiliation, for suffering, or for sin.

children.text: sthāne tu vyayitā satāṃ prabhavati prakhyātaye bhūtaye
children.translated_text: But when expended in the right place by the virtuous, she has the power to bring fame, prosperity,
delight of mind, service to others, and ultimately the attainment of auspiciousness. //
By the one born of the anthill (<s>Vālmīki</s>), King <s>Rāma</s> [was celebrated]; by <s>Vyāsa</s>, the son of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>);
by the poet <s>Kālidāsa</s>, the glorious King <s>Vikramāṅka</s>;
<s>Bhoja</s> by <s>Cittapa</s>, <s>Bilhaṇa</s>, and others; and <s>Karṇa</s> too by the lord of learning (<s>Bhāsa</s>) —

children.text: khyātiṃ yānti nireśvarāḥ kavivaraiḥ sphārairna bherīravaiḥ //
children.translated_text: lordless [kings] attain fame through eminent poets, not through the booming of war-drums! //
Resting in the shade of the tree-like arms of those of great might,
this earth, girdled by oceans, was free from all fear.

children.text: smṛtimapi na te yānti kṣmāpā vinā yadanugrahaṃ
children.translated_text: Yet those kings do not come even to memory without the grace [of poets] —
to that naturally great art of poetry, we offer our salutation. //
Those who were of renowned lineage and foot-service, those who obtained prosperity,
those whose women were like daylight moonbeams in their homes —
the world knows those ornaments of the world as if they were never born,

children.text: bhrātaḥ satkavikṛtya kiṃ stutiśatairandhaṃ jagattvāṃ vinā //
children.translated_text: O brother! Without you, what use are a hundred praises? The world is blind without a good poet! //
What use is the mighty fragrance of musk?
Even the essence of its container is essentially without essence.
Even a garland of flowers does not produce joy
if the goddess of liberation drips with honeyed flow. //
It produces wonder in the mind during the act of composition;
when recited in assemblies, it wins matchless acclaim from the virtuous.
Having attained fame, it brings forth exceedingly noble renown —
what wish does the wish-fulfilling gem of poetry not fulfill? //
He who steals the clear honey of another's poetry, as if stored in a fine receptacle,
and places it in his own lotus —
like a line of ants generated by misplaced fault,
the dark line of his written letters appears [as evidence of his theft]. //
He who is devoted solely to technical rules and definitions, without contact with logic,
not endowed with a mind beautiful through the examination of poetic figures, deprived of training in poetic knowledge —
if from such a one beautiful poetry full of <s>rasa</s> were to emerge,
then a white palace of the king would arise from the blackness of a crow! //
Some master-poet, with his own intelligence as a key,
opening a certain treasure-chest of words bearing curved and graceful forms
from [the realm of] <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquence),
makes it an ornament for the world. //
Some bring the divine words to fruition,
while the deluded ones render them blunt again.
The divine [rain]drops in the mouths of oyster-shells

children.text: tā eva muktā na tu cātakeṣu //
children.translated_text: become pearls — but not in the mouths of <s>Cātaka</s> birds! //
Without a person who knows the toil [of composition],
even the eloquent observe a vow of silence.
Without spring, even the male cuckoos are restrained in speech,
though they are [naturally] quickened by the fifth note. //
The serpent and <s>Rāhu</s>, by the grace of the nectar [they consumed],
received the fierce punishment of severing tongue and head.
'As if' frightened by this, the slanderers
turn away from the nectar of poetic <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). //
One who, with purpose and awareness, speaks the truth that is the sole domain of his own experience,
before those whose minds are deluded by ignorance — will surely become an object of ridicule.

children.text: tadyuktaṃ viduṣo janasya jaḍavajjoṣaṃ nu nāmāsituṃ
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is proper for a wise person to sit silently like a fool.
In the task of describing beauty to the born-blind, what is this futile effort? //
Victorious are the virtuous — who have conquered envy, who are engaged in the welfare of others,
who are established in the prosperity of others, who are distressed by the misfortunes of others,
who are filled with curiosity at hearing the noble tales of great persons,
who are manifest bridges across the ocean of all sins! //
Mute in the slander of others, born-blind at the sight of another's wife,

children.text: paṅguḥ paradhanaharaṇe sa jayati loke mahāpuruṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: lame in the theft of another's wealth — victorious in the world is that great person! //
In prosperity, the hearts of the great become soft as a lotus petal;
in adversity, hard as a mass of great mountain-rock. //
The fate of the noble-minded is twofold, like a cluster of flowers:

children.text: mūrdhni vā sarvalokasya śīryate vana eva vā //
children.translated_text: either upon the head of all the world, or withering in the forest alone. //
They are pained by [receiving] favors; they cannot bear being pitied;
difficult to please even in adversity, always suffering — such are the noble-minded. //
Trees grow by watering, not heaps of stones.

children.text: bhavyo hi dravyatāmeti kriyāṃ prāpya tathāvidhām //
children.translated_text: That which is worthy indeed attains substance when it receives the appropriate action. //
The fear of the lowly is the loss of livelihood; the fear of the middling is death;
but for the highest beings, the greatest fear is dishonor. //

children.text: tāpaṃ hanti sukhaṃ sūte jīvayatyujjvalaṃ yaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: It removes suffering, produces happiness, enlivens brilliant fame —
this is a variety of nectar, rare [to obtain]: the company of the virtuous. //
Like an elixir, cooling, bestowing supreme bliss —
whom indeed does the moonlight of association with the virtuous not delight? //
The auspicious flower of discernment, born from the tree of association with the virtuous —

children.text: rakṣanti ye mahātmāno bhājanaṃ te phalaśriyaḥ //
children.translated_text: those great souls who protect it are the worthy recipients of the glory of its fruit. //
Emptiness becomes fullness, death itself becomes a festival,
adversity shines like prosperity — in the company of the wise. //
Frost is the adversity of the lotus-pond; the deluding wind is <s>Mohana</s> —
victorious in this world is one thing alone: the virtuous person and the company of the virtuous. //
The supreme augmentation of the intellect, the axe for the tree of ignorance,
the expulsion of sorrows — know this to be the company of the virtuous. //
He who has bathed in the cool, pure <s>Gaṅgā</s> of association with the virtuous —

children.text: kiṃ tasya dānaiḥ kiṃ tīrthaiḥ kiṃ tapobhiḥ kimadhvaraiḥ //
children.translated_text: what need has he of charity, of pilgrimages, of austerities, or of sacrifices? //
The hearts of the virtuous are indeed hard — such is my view,
since they are not pierced in the least by the sharp arrow-words of the wicked. //
'Ah! Why is the heart of the virtuous as unfathomable as the ocean?' —
as if angry thus, the Creator, hard to assail, filled [the heart of the virtuous] with the sorrows of others. //

children.text: kāco maṇirmaṇiḥ kāco yeṣāṃ tenye hi dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: For those to whom glass is a gem and a gem is glass, they are [merely] embodied beings.

children.text: santi te sudhiyo yeṣāṃ kācaḥ kāco maṇirmaṇiḥ //
children.translated_text: But those wise ones for whom glass is glass and a gem is a gem — they truly exist. //
A skilled debater can make faults into virtues and virtues into faults,

children.text: śakto vādī na tattathyaṃ doṣā guṇā guṇāḥ //
children.translated_text: but the reality [remains:] faults are faults and virtues are virtues. //
The virtuous, their inner being completely filled with the great weight of a mass of qualities,
attain gravity — if so, what wonder is there in that? //

children.text: svātmanyeva layaṃ yātu tādṛśo guṇināṃ guṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: May such a quality of the virtuous dissolve into their very selves —
[a quality] that, even when proclaimed by itself, is not regarded as [even worth] a blade of grass. //
Even a lowly thing, through contact with a virtuous person, attains distinction.
Through its connection with a flower-garland, even a [blade of] grass is worn upon the head. //
Of the well-rounded, uniform, elevated for the delight of others —
of the virtuous person — like a pair of breasts — whose fall [brings] anyone satisfaction? //

children.text: udeti savitā rakto rakta evāstameti ca /
children.translated_text: The sun rises red and sets red too;
in prosperity and in adversity, the great maintain the same form. //
Like a ball, even falling, the noble one bounces back up;
but the ignoble one falls like a lump of clay. //
Even when struck down by blows of the hand, the ball bounces up again;
for the well-rounded, adversities are generally impermanent. //
Even when fallen, the wise one rises again — but not the dull-witted.
The ball rebounds from a fall — but not the pair of a woman's breasts! //

children.text: apekṣante na ca snehaṃ na pātraṃ na daśāntaram /
children.translated_text: They neither expect affection, nor [consider] the recipient, nor the change of circumstance —
always engaged in the welfare of the world, the excellent are like gem-lamps. //
The virtuous show compassion even to beings devoid of merit,
for the moon does not withhold its moonlight from the outcaste's dwelling. //

children.text: nālokaḥ kriyate sūrye bhūḥ pratīpaṃ na dhāryate /
children.translated_text: The sun is not illuminated [by others]; the earth is not held up in return —
for in the virtuous there exists no expectation of reciprocal favors. //
Even one who does harm generally receives good from the great.
Even the submarine fire that burns — the ocean nurtures it. //

children.text: satpakṣā ṛjavaḥ śuddhāḥ saphalā guṇasevinaḥ dṛṣṭvāpi dṛśyate dṛśyaṃ śrutvāpi śrūyate punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Virtuous in allegiance, upright, pure, fruitful, attendants of merit — even after seeing, the sight is worth seeing again; even after hearing, [it is worth] hearing again.
Truly, in the conduct of the virtuous, repetition is never perceived. //
Virtuous in allegiance, upright, pure, fruitful, attendants of merit —

children.text: tulyairapi guṇaiścitraṃ santaḥ santaḥ śarāḥ śarāḥ //
children.translated_text: though possessing equal qualities — wondrous! — the virtuous are [ever] the virtuous, and arrows are [merely] arrows. //
The lowly desire gain; the noble-minded desire honor.
The diver in the pond seeks fish; the swan desires only clarity. //
A person, naturally straightforward, hearing another's suffering,
being incapable of rendering help, suffers pain in the heart. //

children.text: te vandyāste kṛtinaḥ ślāghyā teṣāṃ hi janmanotpattiḥ /
children.translated_text: They are to be revered, they are accomplished, they are praiseworthy — their birth itself is [truly] a birth,
who, having abandoned their own interests, accomplish the goals of their friends. //
If <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) does not resort to a man who is without deceit, free from greed, sincere,

children.text: yadi nāśrayati naraṃ śrīḥ śrīreva hi vañcitā tatra //
children.translated_text: generous, affectionate, and discerning — then it is Fortune herself who is cheated. //
Health, learning, friendship with the virtuous, birth in a noble family,
and self-reliance — these constitute great wealth for a person, even without riches. //

children.text: svalpāpi sādhusaṃpadbhogyā mahatāṃ na pṛthvyapi khalaśrīḥ /
children.translated_text: Even a small treasure of the virtuous is to be enjoyed by the great; not the wealth of the wicked, vast as the earth.
Only flavorful water quenches thirst — never [the water] of the ocean. //

children.text: na bhavati bhavati ca na ciraṃ bhavati ciraṃ celphalo visaṃvadati /
children.translated_text: It does not arise; or if it arises, it does not last long; or if it lasts long, [the anticipated] result disappoints.
The anger of the virtuous is equal to the affection of the lowly. //

children.text: doṣo guṇāya guṇināṃ mahadapi doṣāya doṣiṇāṃ sukṛtam /
children.translated_text: A fault becomes a virtue for the virtuous; even great merit becomes a fault for the faulty.

children.text: tṛṇamiva dugdhāya gavāṃ dugdhamiva viṣāya sarpāṇām //
children.translated_text: as grass is to the milk of cows, and as milk is to the venom of serpents.

children.text: viṣamagatā api na budhāḥ paribhavamiśrāṃ śriyaṃ hi vāñchanti /
children.translated_text: Even in difficult circumstances, the wise do not desire prosperity mixed with humiliation;

children.text: na pibanti bhaumamambhaḥ sarajasamiti cātakā ete //
children.translated_text: the <s>cātaka</s> birds do not drink earthly water, considering it muddy.
The virtuous mostly perish among the wicked by virtue of their very merit;
it is the parrots that speak clearly who are confined in cages.
The wise assess a person's substance and worthlessness even upon a single encounter;
skilled hands too can determine the weight of a <s>pala</s> by touch alone.

children.text: sujano na yāti vairaṃ parahitanirato vināśakālepi /
children.translated_text: A good person does not become an enemy, being devoted to the welfare of others, even at the time of destruction;
the sandalwood tree, even when cut, perfumes the face of the axe.

children.text: nirguṇamapyanuraktaṃ prāyo na samāśritaṃ jahati santaḥ /
children.translated_text: The good generally do not abandon one who is devoted to them, even though devoid of merit;
the moon bears even its dark spot, though it shares in waxing and waning.

children.text: antyāvasthopi budhaḥ svaguṇaṃ na jahāti jātiśuddhatayā /
children.translated_text: A wise person, even at the final stage, does not abandon his innate quality, by the purity of his nature;
the conch does not give up its whiteness even when swallowed and disgorged by a peacock.

children.text: doṣamapi guṇavati jane dṛṣṭvā guṇarāgiṇo na khidyante /
children.translated_text: Those who love virtue are not distressed upon seeing a fault even in a virtuous person;

children.text: prītyaiva śaśini patitaṃ paśyati lokaḥ kalaṅkamapi //
children.translated_text: with affection, the world regards even the spot upon the moon.
Friendship lasting seven steps arises naturally for those of pure hearts;
how much more for those whose affection is bound by the recounting of each other's virtues!

children.text: spṛhaṇīyāḥ kasya na te sumateḥ saralāśayā mahātmānaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who of good sense would not desire those great souls of straightforward hearts,

children.text: trayamapi yeṣāṃ sadṛśaṃ hṛdayaṃ vacanaṃ tathācāraḥ //
children.translated_text: in whom heart, speech, and conduct are all alike?
Even one devoid of merit, if near a virtuous person, is honored by the world;
through association with a bright eye, even a blind eye receives collyrium.
This is naturally established in the great: indifference to wealth, miserliness toward virtues,
sensitivity to the suffering of others, and great fortitude in their own afflictions.

children.text: atikupitā api sujanā yogena mṛdūbhavanti na tu nīcāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even when greatly angered, good people are softened by gentle means, but not the base;
even hard gold has a means of melting, but not grass.
The virtuous do not count even injury to themselves in their eagerness to do good;
lamp-flames produce light at the cost of burning their own bodies.
The redness of lotuses, the beneficence of the good, and the cruelty of the wicked —

children.text: asatāṃ ca nirdayatvaṃ svabhāvasiddhaṃ triṣu tritayam //
children.translated_text: these three in these three are established by nature.
To give without display, to forgive the lowly, to give without being asked,
and to win others over by virtues — among hundreds, only a few know how.

children.text: guṇini guṇajño ramate nāguṇaśīlasya guṇini paritoṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The connoisseur of merit delights in the meritorious; the one lacking merit finds no satisfaction in the virtuous.
The bee goes from the forest to the lotus; the frog, though dwelling there, does not.

children.text: ādau tu mandamandāni madhye samarasāni ca /
children.translated_text: Associations with the wise are at first slow and gentle, in the middle of equal warmth,
and at the end full of growing affection.
This is a certain kind of austerity
in the hearts of the great, of exalted character:
having done a favor, they remain at a distance,
out of apprehension of a return favor.
If one is compassionate toward a benefactor or one free from envy,
that is merely the lowest level;
he whose mind is merciful even toward one who is hostile

children.text: saghṛṇaṃ yasya manaḥ satāṃ sa dhuryaḥ //
children.translated_text: and has suddenly offended — he is the chief among the good.
In the good, friendship endures at the beginning, middle, and end,
but not in other people;
gold does not change its nature through cutting, striking, grinding, or heating.
Lamps illuminate objects that are present;
but some are the lamps of their lineage —
they illuminate even their long-departed ancestors
by the eminence of their own virtues.
The lofty-souled, most elevated, are able to destroy the mind's affliction, not the base;
rain-clouds alone dispel the heat of mountains' summer forest-fires, not rivers.
Merits become virtues in those who appreciate merit;
those same merits, reaching one devoid of merit, become faults.
Rivers arising from sweet waters
become undrinkable upon reaching the ocean.
The storm does not uproot grasses, which are soft and bend low in every direction;
it assaults only the tall trees that stand erect.
The mighty wreaks havoc only upon the mighty.
A self-possessed person, once his mind is purified by long association with the good,
does not resort to the company of the wicked.
A bee, having found the enchanting petals of a blue lotus,
never settles upon a corpse.
Even deprived of wealth or exiled from his homeland,
a person of noble spirit does not seek the service of the wicked.
Even when tortured by hunger, a lion eats only a little grass [never];
it mostly drinks the hot blood of elephants.

children.text: vitte tyāgaḥ kṣamā śaktau duḥkhe dainyavihīnatā /
children.translated_text: Generosity in wealth, forgiveness when powerful, dignity in suffering,
absence of pretension in good conduct — this is the nature of the great-souled.
The villain indeed plays about in the flimsiness of minor comforts, the impotence of easy joys,
and stumbles into the cholera of despair at the slightest trouble.

children.text: bhavati na satāṃ darpoddāmā na dainyamayī matir-
children.translated_text: The mind of the good is neither wild with pride nor abject with wretchedness,
in happiness and unhappiness alike — for the depth of the profound is hard to overcome.

children.text: svāmye peśalatā guṇe praṇayitā harṣe nirutsekatā
children.translated_text: Gentleness in authority, friendliness toward the virtuous, modesty in joy,

children.text: mantre saṃvṛtatā śrute sumatitā vittodaye tyāgitā /
children.translated_text: discretion in counsel, good sense in learning, generosity upon acquiring wealth,

children.text: sādhau sādaratā khale vimukhatā pāpe paraṃ bhīrutā
children.translated_text: respect for the noble, aversion to the wicked, great fear of sin,
and patience in suffering — these in the great aspire toward the good.
Courage in calamity, forbearance in prosperity,
eloquence in assembly, valor in battle,
devotion to fame, addiction to learning —
these are naturally established in the great-souled.
The wise declare this to be the sign indicating the special mark of greatness:
that the mind of the great, in the presence of happiness or sorrow,
does not fall under the sway of joy or despondency.
Delight in well-spoken words, no elation from prosperity,
action most adept at accomplishing the ends of others,
insatiability for virtues, and reverence for the virtuous —
this is the hidden conduct of the great-souled.
Truly, the virtues of the virtuous, though earned with effort,
become fruitless in the <s>Kali</s> age by the reversal of fate.
Yet this alone is their supreme fruition:
that they burn the hearts of the wicked.
When the villain, with mind given to deception, flattery-laden,
facing his purpose, speaks what is contrived,

children.text: tatsādhavo na na vidanti vidanti kiṃ tu
children.translated_text: the good do not fail to recognize it; they recognize it indeed, but
they are unable to render his feigned affection vain.
The lowest commits sin without remorse;
the one of middling intelligence does so only when fallen upon misfortune, with remorse;
but the virtuous person, even at the cost of life, is not able to transgress good conduct,
just as the ocean does not transgress its shore.

children.text: śuddhiḥ sa eva kulajaśca sa eva dhīraḥ
children.translated_text: He alone is pure, he alone is noble, he alone is steadfast,

children.text: ślāghyo vipatsvapi na muñcati yaḥ svabhāvam /
children.translated_text: praiseworthy is he who does not abandon his nature even in calamity.
Even when heated by the rays of the sun,

children.text: dehaṃ tyajedapi himaṃ na tu śītalatvam //
children.translated_text: snow may abandon its body but not its coolness.
Having experienced the state of begging as a suffering like death,
what is accomplished even by giving in great abundance?
The good, as if mocking wish-fulfilling trees,
give more than what is wished for, without being troubled.
They are the good, the crown-jewels of the circle of the world,
who show goodness toward those who have rendered no service.
