O audacious, arrogant one — no cloud equal to you has ever been seen! //
Opening its mouth, laughing long with your thunder,
O cloud, you rain upon the body of the <s>cātaka</s> (rain-bird).
But for this one, with its beak-tip curved and its long neck [raised],
your [behavior] is merely mockery at the cost of its life! //
Dwelling high upon the peaks of lofty mountains,
taking water from the ocean itself — for the relief of the world's suffering,
casting a long shadow, expansive in form across the vast sky —

children.text: he he megha spṛhayati na te kaḥ kiletthaṃ vratāya //
children.translated_text: ho ho, O cloud, who indeed does not aspire to your vow? //
Dwelling high upon the peaks of lofty mountains,
taking water from the ocean itself — for the relief of the world's suffering,
casting a long shadow, expansive in form across the vast sky —

children.text: he he megha spṛhayati na te kaḥ kiletthaṃ vratāya //
children.translated_text: ho ho, O cloud, who indeed does not aspire to your vow? //
Well done, O mass of auspicious clouds! Well done! This is what the wise should bestow upon the earth.

children.text: konyaḥ kartumalaṃ tavaiva ghaṭate karmedṛśaṃ duṣkaram /
children.translated_text: Who else is able to accomplish such a difficult deed — it befits you alone!
Lightning strikes only those few fields that are suitable for all,
while showers of rain fall on all unsuitable tracts — the burnt sands and wildernesses! //
With frogs sleeping in hollows as if dead, turtles buried in the earth,
large fish rolling about in heaps of thick mud, repeatedly fainting —
to that dried-up lake, the untimely rain-cloud came and performed such a deed
that water was drunk by herds of wild elephants submerged up to their necks! //
That mountains with even slight virtues have grass firmly rooted at their peaks —
and that suddenly these peaks are [washed away] by the grasses —
this is the work of the rain-cloud, raining copiously and unrestrained,
whose water is of an irresistible course. //
One [cloud], having grown, yields sparse, scattered water-drops
and thunders most impetuously — look, from just that meager gain!
Another dances, of incomparable glory and praiseworthy ground — I do not know
between these two, which has the more expansive heart — the <s>cātaka</s> or the cloud? //
Those rain-clouds have departed — dark-bodied like swarms of glistening bees,
by whose splendor even the distinction between land and water was obliterated.
Why do you wander vainly, blinded by thirst, O distressed young <s>cātaka</s>?
This is an autumn cloud — whence even a drop of water for you? //
'Let us see what this one does' — with minor cloudy feats,
disdained from afar out of arrogance, [yet] impelled to action by powerful ministers —
having gained free range, and unable now to be checked, hurling thunderbolts,
alas, the swollen cloud, that enemy, has burned the mountain village! //

children.text: garjitvā bahu saṃnirudhya gaganaṃ pracchādya diṅmaṇḍalaṃ
children.translated_text: Having thundered greatly, having sealed the sky, having covered the horizons,
having fashioned a body beautifully dark like split fragments of sapphire —
even when the season of rain-clouds arrived, the rain-cloud withheld its water

children.text: cañcūśrātakapotakasya sakalā siktā na yena svayam //
children.translated_text: and did not itself wet even the entire beak of a thirsty pigeon! //
Here, the sudden cloud, spreading across the empty sky without counsel,
has thus swelled forth in a village suited to its own bold, natural deeds.
People could not tell the difference
between the mud-bearing street-streams, pure and clear, and the flood-waters of the river-currents. //

children.text: re meghāḥ svaśarīradānaguru kiṃ bauddhaṃ yaśo na śrutaṃ
children.translated_text: Ho, clouds! Have you not heard the Buddhist fame of self-sacrifice?

children.text: yaṣmābhiḥ kimu pārijātacaritaṃ nākarṇitaṃ vā kvacit /
children.translated_text: Or have you nowhere heard the tale of the <s>Pārijāta</s> (wish-fulfilling tree)?
That in giving this easily-obtained water, while you thunder
and rush impetuously across the sky, you feel not even shame? //

children.text: sthāne varṣati naiva garjati vṛthā klāntiṃ haratyañjasā
children.translated_text: He rains in the right place, never thunders in vain, and readily removes weariness
of the fields whose luster is withered by heat — a bringer of welfare upon the earth.
Whatever auspicious density he holds in his heart, he enacts with radiance —
may this true cloud, of unfailing appearance and richly dark luster, flourish! //
The ocean does not thunder, though its fame is swelled by granting the desires sought by the lord of the three worlds,
and it is filled with priceless gems and blazing with tongues of submarine fire.
Yet this cloud, of vulgar nature, whose distortion is removed by a mere trifle of that water,
hurling water into the void, thunders proudly — [this one] of uncounted [and meager] resources! //
The ocean does not maintain the boundary called the shore
as much as it maintains this other one: 'The thirsty shall not be helped.' //

children.text: gavādīnāṃ payonyedyuḥ sadyo vā dadhi jāyate /
children.translated_text: From cows and others, milk [turns to] curds either the next day or immediately.
But even to this day, the milk-ocean has not changed — whence alteration in the great? //
Although the ocean, by its clear nature, reveals gems,
do not think in your mind, 'It is only knee-deep.' //
He into whose mouth not even a drop of water falls for the supplicants —
wretched! Even that ocean is called [merely] a 'collection of rivers'! //

children.text: yātu nāśaṃ samudrasya mahimā sa bhuvi śrutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Let the fame of the ocean, celebrated on earth, go to ruin!
The submarine fire (<s>Vāḍava</s>), tormented by hunger and thirst, was not satisfied even singly by it! //
When the ocean exists — which distributed the nectar-essence and saved the gods from death —

children.text: kasya sphuranti hṛdaye grīṣmataḍākā bhuvi varākāḥ //
children.translated_text: in whose heart do the wretched summer ponds on earth even flicker? //
That <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) bears the moon upon his crest,
that <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) is the lord of <s>Śrī</s> (fortune),
that these immortals are divine —
all these are but drops of that [ocean's] glory. //
Your saltiness is indeed a virtue,
by which no one approaches you. /
O ocean, why do you bear before you the <s>cakra</s> (discus)
in the terrifying form of sea-creatures? //
Setting aside the enmity born of the stealing of <s>Lakṣmī</s>,
and not brooding on that churning of the mountain — /
the great ocean gave shelter to <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu);
indeed, the conduct of the steadfast and wise is free from envy. //
O lord of waters, bearing gems that surpass the moon's radiance below,
yet carrying grass upon your head — /
O lord, there is in truth no [other] lord [like you]:
gems are gems, and grass is grass. //
Let those wretched, narrow-natured ponds
hate summer and long for the arrival of clouds. /
But for the ocean, with its playful innocent fish and immovable mountain-like
unmoved belly of water, both [summer and rains] are of no concern. //
Its pebbles are gems, its fish is <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) dwelling in the waters, its <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Splendor) is a water-goddess,
its clusters of pearls are sand, its coral creepers are moss, its water is nectar. /
On its shores are <s>Kalpa</s>-trees (wish-fulfilling trees) — what more? Even the name 'mine of gems'
is a delight to the ears from afar, yet up close, thirst is not quenched! //
Let the ocean's water dispel the fatigue
of those whose minds are set ablaze by forest fire — that is far [from possible]. /
Let this much be: if only by drops of water the tongue

children.text: dandahyate dviguṇatāṃ ca na yāti tṛṣṇā //
children.translated_text: is not scorched, and thirst does not double! //
O abode of <s>makara</s>s (sea-creatures), do not despise these gems
with the harsh blows of wave-tossed rocks! /

children.text: kiṃ kaustubhena vihito bhavato na nāma
children.translated_text: Was not even <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Being) made by the <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem]
to extend his hand in supplication? //
We are greatly ashamed — many
travelers enter this body of water, /
and the dogs on the nearby shore, carried on their shoulders,
have eyes eager for water, with their thirst intensified! //
This ocean, notorious even among women and children as undrinkable,
is guarded from the thirsty from afar by its very unpotability. /
Having seen [it guarded by] terrible <s>makara</s>s (crocodiles) and frightful
waves upon waves — why do you still try to frighten? //
Shame, shame, shame on this shameless ocean,
whose travelers are utterly exhausted as if in a desert! /
With long tongues protruding from throats dried by the burning of thirst,
the wretched ones go along the shore with eyes rolling [in agony]. //
If it is churned by the armies of gods and demons,
if it is filled with waters from clouds and rivers, /
if it is drunk by the submarine mare-fire —
the ocean is neither agitated nor diminished. //
Where <s>Maināka</s> and other mountains have taken refuge, terrified of <s>Indra</s>,
whence the blessed sun of fierce rays rises, and where he sets, /

children.text: śete kvāpi nilīya yasya jagatāṃ kukṣyekadeśe patir-
children.translated_text: where the lord of all worlds sleeps, concealed somewhere in a corner of its belly —
who is able to match the majesty of this ocean's depth? //
Having benefited [the world] with <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), gems, <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu), the crescent moon,
and nectar for all the gods, even for the enemy of <s>Kāma</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — /
how else could [its fame] stand, heavy with the burden of glory,

children.text: yadi na mathanāyāsaṃ dhīraḥ saheta payonidhiḥ //
children.translated_text: if the steadfast ocean did not endure the toil of churning? //

children.text: viṣamabhimukhaṃ muktaṃ raudraṃ diśo daśa saṃśritāḥ
children.translated_text: Poison was released — terrifying, facing all ten directions;
enticement was offered in the form of moon, trees, and gems. /

children.text: kimiva na kṛtaṃ nanthārambhe śaṭhena payodhinā
children.translated_text: What was not done by the treacherous ocean at the beginning of the churning?
Yet even so, the skilled gods did not relent without obtaining the nectar. //
If by your depth and greatness, time itself
undertakes the display of fitting virtues — what then comes after? /
O ocean, why these waves that achieve no completion?
Desist! — not even a little of this water belongs to the rivers. //
While this one [the submarine fire] of blazing body dwells
in the lap of [the ocean], face averted, even for a moment — /
the thirst of the <s>aurvāgni</s> (submarine fire) is not removed even when wealth abounds;
let the glory of this cruel ocean perish! //
Alas, this is the most ignoble nature of the lord of rivers:
that its brilliant gems, its qualities polished long and carefully, /
are cast out ceaselessly and violently by the dull, useless [waves],
having arrived from outside and found a place, becoming one with them! //
Here, one [the ocean] from whose pot all were born, coveting the crest-jewel,
yet unable to fill even a cupped handful for the thirsty with its waters — /
O ocean, why do you torment by deafening the cavities of our ears
with your deep, dense roars boasting of your own greatness? //

children.text: rūkṣaṃ kṣāramapeyamatra salilaṃ labdhvā paraṃ tapyate
children.translated_text: The water here is coarse, salty, and undrinkable — one who obtains it is greatly disappointed;
due to fear of serpents and crocodiles, it cannot be entered even by the healthy. /

children.text: tatkiṃ pāntha payodhināmani marau tṛṣṇāvimūḍho bhavān-
children.translated_text: Then why, O traveler, confused by the mirage of thirst in the desert, do you seek the ocean —
running vainly toward the heaps of pure gems concealed within? //
This bearing of all the world's three waters is yours;
this splendor is yours, O dwelling of waters; this is your great magnanimity. /
Yet, having served you with your many-breaking, terrifying body —
O sinner, the heat-quarrel is somehow quenched at the rock-stream of the shore-mountain! //
Let this [ocean] scatter great mountains with its surging waves,

children.text: śabdairvā badhirīkarotu kakubho dhattāṃ ca vistīrṇatām /
children.translated_text: or deafen the quarters with sounds arising from the play of tides, or assume vastness. /
What equality can the boasting ocean achieve with even a small lake

children.text: kiṃ sāmyaṃ pratanoḥ karotu sarasopyabdhiḥ kṛtāḍamabaraḥ //
children.translated_text: that quenches the excessive thirst of travelers whose bodies are scorched by the sun's heat? //
By one of supreme valor, the incomparable treasure-house of nectar was given to the supplicant;
<s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) too, and the great gem [<s>Kaustubha</s>], the moon, the <s>Kalpa</s>-tree, and the divine cow —  /
yet, cursed with salty waters, the ocean is still called [generous] — ah,
this world, counting virtue as a straw, is single-mindedly intent on grasping faults! //
'Alas! Even though I dwell on the shore, seeing my fruitless former burden [of water],
these creatures go elsewhere every day to quench their thirst.' /
Thus, as if from the sorrow born of bearing the excessive burden of useless water,
the ocean, I think, daily offers its own body into the submarine fire. //
By guarding boundaries, by protecting the great kings of the earth,
by being the resting-place of <s>Madhusūdana</s> (Viṣṇu) for a long time — whatever little was gained, /
befitting its own depth, the ocean, in the panic of the churning-agony,
surrendering the nectar to the gods in haste — alas, all that was squandered! //
Wondrous is the <s>vaḍavānala</s> (submarine fire)! Wondrous is the ocean!
Contemplating the extraordinary deeds of each, the mind trembles. /
The one, sheltered [in the ocean] and voracious, drinking [its] waters, never attained satisfaction;

children.text: anyasyāpi mahātmano na vapuṣaḥ svalpopi jātaḥ śramaḥ //
children.translated_text: yet for the other, the great-souled [ocean], not even the slightest exhaustion of body occurred. //

children.text: nodvegaṃ yadi yāsi yadyavahitaḥ karṇaṃ dadāsi kṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: If you are not upset, if you lend your ear for a moment,

children.text: tvāṃ pṛcchāmi yadambudhe kimapi tanniścitya dehyuttaram /
children.translated_text: I ask you, O ocean, something — consider it and give an answer. /
That you are seen sighing, sharpened to the extreme by the remorse of despair —
is it from the thirsty travelers, or is it more from the burning of the submarine fire? //
On this side sleeps <s>Keśava</s> (Viṣṇu); on that side, the hosts of his enemies;
on this side, the virtues of the mountains seeking shelter lie. /
On this side, the submarine fire together with all the dissolution-fires —
ah, vast, mighty, and burden-bearing is the body of the ocean! //
To <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> (Viṣṇu) [it gave] <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), to <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva) the fresh moon,
to the Thunderbolt-wielder (<s>Indra</s>) even <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> (the divine horse) — where is that reckoned? /

children.text: tṛṣṇārtāya svamapi munaye yaddadāti sma dehaṃ
children.translated_text: That it gave its own body to a sage tormented by thirst —
who else in all the worlds is a greater <s>bodhisattva</s> (awakened being) than the ocean? //
If the ocean, gleaming with gems, scattering its waves with the winds,
were to be turned toward the blocked shore — /
that [criticism] belongs to fault-seekers, to those of reversed fortune;
not even slightly [does it detract] from his generosity. //
Those very [drops] that constantly roll about within, taken in by the ocean
as they fall from the clouds in countless numbers, embraced by the encircling waves — /
clearly the ocean transforms the water-drops into pearls and gems;
generally, one who is honored by a master, even if small, is esteemed. //
May it be well with the coral creepers, flowers, and gems!
May the rows of pearl-oysters be auspicious! /
I have obtained every fruit of the ocean,
for I was not torn apart by the terrible sea-creatures! //
Having taken water from the mouths of rivers on all sides —
what has this dreadful ocean achieved thereby? /
It was made salty, offered to the submarine fire,
and deposited in the hollow belly of the netherworld! //
One who, when the time comes, does not seize the great gem, being foolish, /
later suffers, seeing it gone into another's hand. //
That which, entering inside, is split according to the [color of the] object placed [near it] — /
what kind of purity is that, of the dull crystal stone? //

children.text: sphaṭikasya guṇo yosau sa evāyāti doṣatām /
children.translated_text: That very quality of crystal becomes a fault:
it takes on, through its transparency, the appearance even of the impure. //
By which the value of a piece of stone [becomes] the [whole] earth —
that is the display of the unfading brilliance of [the gem's] radiance. //
The one who, from desire for wealth, grasps the tip of a dry, thin blade of straw —
the foolish employ even that 'straw-gem' for the protection of the foot [as a sandal]! //
Born of a good lineage, endowed with fine qualities, well-rounded,
embraced by one whose qualities equal the relief of heat [i.e., the sandalwood] — /
see — the necklace, lovely to behold, is nonetheless
cast out by the pair of high breasts! //
If a gem fit for setting in golden ornaments
is bound [instead] in tin — /

children.text: na sa virauti na cāpi hi śobhate
children.translated_text: it neither shines nor sparkles,
and the blame falls upon the one who set it. //
Better the natural darkness of the emerald,

children.text: tyajati jātu nijāṃ prakṛtiṃ na yaḥ /
children.translated_text: which never abandons its own nature, /
than the purity of the crystal — shame on it! —
which takes on the form of whatever is placed near it. //
In this great abundance of gem-hood, O friend <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem),
be a [mere] stone, do not become a gem! /
For today such gems prevail in the world
whose only ornament is the skill of grasping straws! //
Though falling to the ground, though grey with dust,
though scorned by the born-blind wicked — /
the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) never abandons
its inner glory of being worshipped by the three worlds. //
O <s>Cintāmaṇi</s>, if you have not been held on the head by any lord on earth,

children.text: mūrdhnā dhṛtosi yadi mā sma tato viṣīdaḥ /
children.translated_text: do not grieve on that account. /
Indeed, there is no one whose crown
has the seed of merit worthy of the fortune of bearing you. //
The <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) and the straw-gem — by the Creator,
gem-hood was made the same for both! /
The one, distressed, gives manifold desired things to the supplicant;
the other, grasping a dry straw-blade, feels no shame. //
Surrounded by hundreds of desires, fit for the crown of a world-lord,
yet brought low by [mere] straws, placed among rocks — /
though it enters the sight of those who have discernment —
this <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> rolls about in mountain caves, forlorn. //
One handles it eagerly, gazes at it delicately again and again,
conceals with unmatched rapture [the thought] 'This is some great gem!' /
Having obtained from somewhere a piece of glass, like a coating [of value],
the wretched fool endures extreme contempt — alas! //
Filling the circle of directions long with clusters of rays —
O brother, why have you been displayed here in a cave to no purpose? /
Who here knows fully your innately great value,
O emerald gem, in this burnt village of wretched, contemptuous folk? //
For someone [the gem] is far away; for another, dull-witted, who does not know its inner worth;

children.text: mānī kopi na yācate mṛgayate kopyalpamalpāśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: yet another, being proud, does not beg; another of small ambition seeks only a little. /
Thus the touchstone of the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem), brilliant with the line of generosity,
addicted to granting what is asked, was never applied in places difficult to test by skill. //

children.text: ye gṛhṇanti haṭhāttṛṇāni maṇayo ye vāpyayaḥpiṇḍikāṃ
children.translated_text: Those gems that forcibly seize straws, and those that [attract] iron lumps —
they have been seen everywhere as burnt gems, long since discounted! /

children.text: no jāne kimabhāvataḥ kimathavā daivādiha śrūyate
children.translated_text: I do not know whether from non-existence, or whether from fate — it is heard here

children.text: nāmāpyatra na tādṛśasya tu maṇe ratnāni gṛhṇāti yaḥ //
children.translated_text: that there is not even the name of that kind of gem which grants [true] jewels. //
The pearls that the great waves cast forth from the depths of the ocean
roll about on the shores, with pure luster, as if with hearty laughter —
yet for those very [gems] diminishing from the ocean, clinging to other shores,
there are indeed merchants addicted to acquisition [who gather] the jewels. //
This <s>māṇikya</s> (ruby) is of great price, honored on the face of the earth, radiant, of noble birth —
seeing it from afar, surely some misfortune-doctrine retreats far away!
Thus, through elaborate delusions, set up by someone to avert calamity,

children.text: nnante dṛṣṭaḥ sa eva vraṇaśataparuṣaḥ kopi pāṣāṇakhaṇḍaḥ //
children.translated_text: in the end it was found to be just some rough piece of stone, scarred with a hundred wounds! //

children.text: yāmaḥ svasti tavāstu rohaṇagire mattaḥ sthitipracyutā
children.translated_text: We depart — may you fare well, O <s>Rohana</s> mountain! 'Fallen from their station on my account,

children.text: vartiṣyanta ime kathaṃ kathamiti svapnepi maivaṃ kṛthāḥ /
children.translated_text: how will these manage?' — do not think thus, even in a dream!
O illustrious one, your gems are we; if we, having obtained eminence through you,

children.text: te śṛṅgāraparāyaṇāḥ kṣitibhujo maulau kariṣyanti naḥ //
children.translated_text: then those kings, devoted to elegance, will place us upon their crowns. //

children.text: uccairuccaratu ciraṃ cīrī vartmani taruṃ samāruhya /
children.translated_text: Let the cricket chirp loudly and long, having climbed a tree on the path!
When the quality of sound pervades the quarters, the conch alone is the ground of esteem. //
The conch is but a remnant of bone, cracked, dead —
that it breathes by being breathed into, [that is] true indeed.
But the sound it produces is not [merely] a sound

children.text: śravyo na yo yo na sadarthaśaṃsī //
children.translated_text: unworthy of hearing, nor one that does not declare true meaning. //
Having given up its life-breath, the virtues fitting to its whiteness
were attained through the special contact of mouths in the world.
Those conches, resounding with the sound of great splendor —
those noble-hearted ones in whose lives [such glory] arises are [truly] powerful. //

children.text: dhīraḥ śrotrasukhāvahopi sadṛśaḥ satyaṃ paraṃ maṅgalaṃ
children.translated_text: Majestic, pleasing to the ear, dignified, truly the highest auspiciousness —

children.text: kvāpi grāmasurāṅgaṇe sa tu lasansaṃdhyāsu śaṅkhadhvaniḥ /
children.translated_text: yet that conch-sound, shining at the twilight hours in some village temple courtyard,
is drowned out by the long-drawn howl rising from the outstretched necks of stout, inebriated hounds —
a sound that provokes imitative, vulgar bursts of village laughter! //
Though born from the ocean, the mine of gems, yet being diminished,
reduced even to the thinness of a dry bone-remnant,
buffeted even by forceful blowing breaths —
the conch, pure of heart, speaks only of auspiciousness. //
Conches exist by the thousands, battered by the ocean's wave-clusters,
rolling on the shores, spotting the ground with hundreds of fragments.

children.text: ekaḥ kopi sa pāñcajanya udabhūdāścaryabhūtaḥ satāṃ
children.translated_text: Yet one alone, that <s>Pāñcajanya</s>, arose as a wonder among the good,
which is filled by the breaths of <s>Madhus</s>'s foe [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], capable of bearing the burden of cosmic dissolution. //
Fulfilling all directions with its proud humming, born too from the milk-ocean,
kissing the lips of <s>Govinda</s>, with a body more beautiful than the full moon's orb —

children.text: śrīreṣā sahajā guṇāḥ kimaparaṃ bhaṇyanta ete hi yat-
children.translated_text: this innate <s>Śrī</s> (splendor), these virtues — what more can be said? Yet
O <s>Pāñcajanya</s>, for the crookedness in your heart, we are exceedingly ashamed! //
Better to be without <s>Śrī</s> (beauty/Lakṣmī) than to have equality with another's <s>Śrī</s> —
thus, when the <s>kairava</s> (night-lotus) blooms, the [day-]lotus closes into a bud. //
This is certainly a fault of the lotus — its contact with <s>Lakṣmī</s> —
that it turns its face away from the moon, the abode of a multitude of virtues. //
Many hollows within, many thorns without —
how could the virtues of the lotus-stalk not be fragile? //
O lotus, among your many and long virtues
that are white [pure], what is the reason for concealment?
There is indeed [a reason] — if the ignoble one sees them,
<s>Lakṣmī</s>, as if frightened, does not set foot [there]. //
O land-lotus, gather your thorns,
display with delight your origin from mud-filled [waters],
and fix your resolve upon contact with water —
whereby you attain the status of being the abode of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī). //
Though there is this addiction to gambling in its eyes, dense passion in its heart,
and intoxicating arrogance from the honey-wine in its face —
the lotus is nevertheless the supreme abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s>;
that wretchedness is indeed misfortune — that it [should be associated] with these! //
Though lotuses and the like are possessed of many virtues, yet at night
they do not perish from separation with the sun.
That sluggishness born of their origin in mud-mixed pools of water,
is [their] greater expansive [flaw] — acknowledged by all three worlds. //
O lotus, distinguish <s>Lakṣmī</s> who bears the mark of skill,

children.text: jṛmbhā jahīhi calatāṃ ca vimuñca kiṃcit /
children.translated_text: give up yawning and release some of [your] fickleness!
Gladden the swarms of bees that have come with hopes,
and with a friendly <s>Vidhi</s> (fate/Creator) present, arrange this as you wish. //
O lotus, hear constantly my words,
which I speak to you with some affection.
With this pure radiance, with bees or with virtues,
why do you attain the highest loveliness — or is it because of the thorn-tipped stalk? //
Contract now, O lotus-flower, abandon your splendor!
See, the moon, the abode of faults, now rises.
When the crooked one prevails, upon deliberation, step by step,
concealment is indeed fitting for the virtuous. //
Though its threads are breaking, though it has come to have many thorns,
though it is full of holes, though born of wretched mud,
though its wealth is enjoyed by bees — still the lotus
always attains blossoming when its friend [the sun] rises. //
Let there be lotus-clusters resounding with the dense humming
of honey-craving swarms of bees jostling together!
That [unique] lotus from the navel of the Upholder of the Earth [<s>Viṣṇu</s>],
upon which <s>Brahmā</s> himself sings in super-melodious tones, is indeed something apart! //
Dispelling heat, warm-hearted, beautiful, fully awakened,
delighting in the affection of its friend [the sun], bearing a multitude of good virtues,
gratifying the bees by the gift of its own body —
it is fitting, O <s>Kamalā</s> (Lakṣmī), that your abode is in this lotus. //
Neither born from mud, nor addicted to dwelling with the dull,
your body anointed with a luster that steals the brilliance of gems, O land-lotus —
if cruel fate had not made lightness of heart your [flaw],
you alone would have been the supreme abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s> here. //
Many clusters of lotuses have arisen on the surfaces of lakes,
which have become metaphors for the faces of beautiful women resembling the lord of the night [moon].
Yet that one great <s>Mahāpadma</s> arose from the navel of the enemy of <s>Bhūmi</s>'s [foe],
which attained the status of being the birthplace of the originator of the three worlds' creation. //
Access to its flower was deftly stolen by the fragrance-craving [bees],
entry within its expanse was denied by its tightly closed bud-state.
Having thus been brought to despair, with movement arrested, the simple-minded one at dusk —

children.text: padmena śrīmatāpi prasabhamubhayato bhraṃśitaḥ paśya bhṛṅgaḥ //
children.translated_text: see! The bee is forcibly dislodged from both sides even by the splendid lotus. //
Brother lotus, endure contraction for a little while;

children.text: saiva prabhāte śobhā te bhāte dinakare bhavet //
children.translated_text: that very splendor of yours shall return at dawn when the sun shines. //
Having reached a downward state, the lotus-stalks, stained with mud,
are dragged by the virtuous-less fishermen and their sprouts revealed. //
Those sprouts become lotuses, endowed with virtues, by the proud [sun];
borne upon the head [in worship], they close [at night] as if of dull nature. //
In the desert there is simply no water; if with great difficulty some is obtained,

children.text: tatkaṭu stokamuṣṇaṃ ca na karoti vitṛṣṇatām //
children.translated_text: it is bitter, scanty, and warm — it does not quench thirst. //
The drop of water falling from the eager beak of the restless <s>cātaka</s> (rain-bird)
is beyond the reach of the desert.
But that [bird] is now made otherwise [satisfied]
by the cloud, the friend of the rainy season, with its waters. //
O traveler, in this desert, well-named,
possessing materials useful for the accomplishment of churning —
how contrary this is, for what is seen there
is a well, and in it water easily obtained! //
What more is there to say about this desert?
Do not let go, O traveler, for the earth is ever kind to those who seek refuge.
By you, greedy for the bait of a drop of water,
has been seen [only] the burning expanse of sand. //
Good trees, with bodies surrounded by the wealth of abundant leaves and flower-burdens,
bowed with the weight of fruit,
with great branches sheltering hundreds of sweetly chirping birds —
he who seeks such [trees] in the desert, that one is a fool. //
Devoid of water, trees, and grass — 'For the weary travelers,
I am utterly unable to render any service' —

children.text: iti na paramabhīkṣṇaṃ nānuśete na yāvac-
children.translated_text: thus thinking, the desert does not rest, but unceasingly
deploys deceptive mirages to draw them toward illusory waters. //
Gone with all speed, wandering and wandering, and the ground heaving up —
then after a long while, sighing deeply, standing pitifully still —

children.text: kimiva na kṛtaṃ pānthenetthaṃ tathāpi śaṭho maruḥ
children.translated_text: what has the traveler not done? Yet the cruel desert,
harsh by nature, alas, has not yielded even the slightest moisture. //
Here a terrifying flock of crows, here the deeds of owls,
here vultures and the like, here the clan of herons and jays —
in this cremation ground, barren of all virtues, on the ruined tree,

children.text: api dvitrāḥ kecinna khalu kalavācaḥ śakunayaḥ //
children.translated_text: are there not at least two or three sweet-voiced birds? //
Are you confused, or have you gone mad, that in an instant you are observed

children.text: punarapi punaḥ prekṣāpūrvā na kācana te kriyā /
children.translated_text: and again and again no action of yours is well-considered?
Knowing it yourself to be waterless, yet entering the desert plain,
you desire to obtain cool, sweet water, O traveler! //
He who endures suffering for others' sake, who is sweet even when broken,
whose transformation is indeed approved by all here —

children.text: na saṃprāpto vṛddhiṃ yadi sa bhṛśamakṣetrapatitaḥ
children.translated_text: if he has not attained growth, being sown in barren ground,
is that the fault of sugarcane, or rather the worthlessness of the desert-born [soil]? //
Heat upon those sheltered under your trees and vines, rejection by travelers,
truly due to the intensity of their thirst — O desert, your anger brings no profit.
But this is a great gain: that ordinary rain-clouds, booming with pride
at their lordship over a drop of water, gird themselves for your aid! //
Thus, even by the Creator [you were] made incapable of rendering any service whatsoever —

children.text: kāmaṃ mopakṛthāstatastava maro vācyaṃ na dhīro bhava /
children.translated_text: very well, do not help me — O desert, nothing may be said [against you]; be patient.
But by generating from afar the deception of clouds through mirages,
you attract with love even others whose minds are swooning with thirst — for this you are to be pitied. //
Are the mangoes not lovely, their heads bowed with the burden of fruit, dispelling heat?
Are the cool-shadowed banana trees, the fragrant blossoming <s>campakas</s>, not [beautiful]?
These have been licked away and overgrown again by fierce, unchecked young camels —

children.text: śamyo bhrāmyasi mūḍha nirmaruti kiṃ mithyaiva martuṃ marau //
children.translated_text: O fool, why do you wander in the windless [desert], vainly courting death? //

children.text: jalāntarāṇi śvabhreṣu tiṣṭhantu kvāpi yāntu vā /
children.translated_text: Let the waters within the wells remain wherever they are, or let them go —
when the celestial river flows, the ocean is the limit. //
Where is the hollow reed, and where the sugarcane? Yet both look alike!
They were created for the deception of those whose minds lack discrimination. //

children.text: nāsya bhāragrahe śaktirna ca vāhaguṇaḥ kṛṣau /
children.translated_text: He has no strength to bear loads, nor the virtue of a draft-animal in plowing —
yet the temple-bull eats the finest [food] all the same. //
The crocodile, reaching its own domain, drags even the lord of elephants;
that very one, displaced from its position, is humiliated even by a dog. //
Better a blow from the paw of a lion,
with its tail raised high, its mane-shaking terrifying —
than the mounting of a jackal! //
The sandalwood tree, whose sole essence is fragrance, fruitless, is [still] attended upon;

children.text: kva gato mṛgo na jīvatyanudinamaśnaṃstṛṇāni vividhāni /
children.translated_text: the serpents that feed on wind are its attendants — such is the decree of fate. //
Where has the deer gone that does not live, eating various grasses day after day?
But the livelihood of the lion, who eats [only] the elephant slain by itself, is truly rare. //
Crooked, lying in no [proper] bed, hollow within, having many difficult knots —

children.text: na tadanukṛtaṃ manāgapi na vā jalaṃ sucirasevitaiḥ śītam /
children.translated_text: even <s>Viśvakarman</s> (the divine craftsman) cannot straighten a piece of bad wood. //

children.text: andhīkṛte kudīpaiḥ pratyuta dhūmena me nayane //
children.translated_text: Not even the slightest benefit has been produced by those [wicks] long attended — nor even cool water;
rather, my eyes have been blinded by the smoke of wretched lamps! //
When shall we see with clear eyes that ruined shop
where wish-fulfilling gems and glass beads have their virtues and defects reversed? //
He who touches a lamp, mistaking it for a bright <s>campaka</s> bud —
apart from the burning stain of soot, what else can happen to him? //
The ocean, with peaks heaped high, crested, blazing with clusters of leaping <s>aurva</s>-fire —
it is to be crossed by someone, but this pile of copper coins is not a city! //
When <s>Śeṣa</s>, with his hood-gems shining, powerful, with many heads,
who would entreat wretched little worms to bear the burden of the earth? //

children.text: yadi jaladaninadamuditāsta eva mūḍhā na nṛtyeyuḥ //
children.translated_text: if those very fools, delighted by the rumble of clouds, would not dance! //
In autumn, the night — whose mass of darkness is dispelled by hundreds of rays of the full moon —
cannot fill even the semblance of day, though the sun is hidden behind clouds. //
Though <s>Madana</s> (Kāma, the god of love) has a retinue soft and charming in appearance, this one thing alone is unfitting:
that he has placed on his banner the <s>makara</s> (sea-monster), whose mouth is terrifying with fangs. //
O goldsmith of good intellect, salutations to you!
In matters difficult to cross, you have repeatedly tested —
a golden ornament together with a stone,
that you have placed both these on the same balance-scale! //
That pot in the blind well is indeed made round,
yet is unable to remove [even a drop of] your grace.
Your lowly conduct has been sealed by you
who accept the water-drops from its mouth. //
If the centipede, despite having a hundred feet, is unable
to cross even a cow's hoof-print,
why do we dispute the two-footed <s>Hanumān</s>'s
crossing of the ocean? //
No fondness for the acquisition of a noble lineage,
no regard for the collection of great virtues,
no mention even of the provision of fruit in the search —
what is your home now worth, O arrow of the hunter? //
Of a blade of grass, a jewel, a human being, and one like him —
what of the vast ambition of both is to be said?
With their slender parts like the tip of a grass-blade,
both are completed in grasping and bestowing. //
Brother, O goldsmith, skilled in the arrangement of efforts
for making ornaments of golden figurines with wonderful designs —
cease your labor here today: in a golden vessel,
there is great profit to be had from applying inferior color! //
Who here has not long been deceived
by the water-drop held on the tip of a slender grass-blade, mistaking it for a pearl?
That one of reversed vision [was deceived] — but this world,
we here are conscious beings. //
O serpent (<s>dandaśūka</s>)! Though it is improper, the Lord, out of affection,
truly brings you to the station of an anklet.
But the tinkling sounds that attract and honor swarms of bees —

children.text: kiṃ śiñjitāni bhavataḥ kṣama eṣa kartum //
children.translated_text: is this [serpent] capable of producing those? //
O goldsmith, you have come here to sell
wares suitable for the ears.
That this has not yet been heard in the village —
surely the village chief has unpierced ears! //
We fashion those lofty mountains, indeed,
whose vigor is churned away at the reversal of wings' destruction.
Is it proper even for the submarine fire (<s>aurvāgni</s>), when provoked,
to endure the churning of the ocean, even though it is of fiery nature? //
How wondrous that this ocean is magnified
by the fullness of cloud-torrents and river-currents!
But you, O small well, serve the needy
by squeezing out the hollow of your belly — that indeed is greatness! //
Shame on the submarine fire (<s>vāḍava</s>), who, when implored, approaches the enemy
for the filling of his own belly!
Shame also on the ocean, who even with the waters
of such an enemy cannot fulfill his desire! //
Desiring to protect the young ones nestled in the nest,
having quickly taken water from the river in the cup of her wing,
the female <s>kopoṭī</s> (dove) repeatedly sprinkled the forest fire —

children.text: snigdho jano na khalu cintayate svapīḍām //
children.translated_text: an affectionate being does not consider its own suffering. //
The crow, fickle by nature, yet of pure conduct,
having obtained food, calls both his own kind and others.
Even over an elephant carcass with skin, bones, and flesh,
the dog, miserly by nature, hates and attacks others. //

children.text: ādāyi vāri yata eva jahāti bhūyas-
children.translated_text: He who takes water from the very place where he releases it again —

children.text: tatraiva yaḥ sa jaladaḥ prathamo jaḍānām /
children.translated_text: that cloud is the foremost among the foolish.
But he who desires to take back what was vomited — that very thing —
that lord of streams (ocean) is the shameless caravan-leader. //
Even though we deliberate in many ways, we do not understand —
by what names shall we designate those of great intellect,
for whom, in ascertaining the truth of gold — the ornament of the entire world —
stones are the supreme authority? //
The faces of all luminous ones have not been dimmed,

children.text: nāstaṃ tamo na ca kṛto bhuvanopakāraḥ /
children.translated_text: darkness has not set, nor has any benefit been rendered to the world.
'I am the son of the Sun' — by what merit will you, O <s>Śani</s> (Saturn),
convince the worlds, without an oath? //
The farmer made a scarecrow to protect the crops —
behold, this straw-man is an image of himself!
Surely the stiff, inactive, and motionless one's
cows, deer, and birds will eat the grain again. //
Whose eyes are unblinking and wide — except in the world of celestial beings,

children.text: lokādṛte jagati te api vai gṛhītvā /
children.translated_text: indeed, even they have acquired [this trait] —
you who stretch your mouth wide open at a morsel, in darkness,
O fool, did you not see the clear hook inside? //
From birth onward, O ill-born dust,

children.text: pāṃso tvayā yadi kṛtaṃ vada tattvametat /
children.translated_text: have you done even a particle of good? Tell the truth!
For whose sake you were raised by the charioteer of fire (wind) —
O wicked one, do that: stain this universe! //
Even if one should waver from manliness, even if one should fall below,
even if one should be servile, even if one were great —
yet one would uplift this universe — such a path
has been manifested in the directions by some <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person). //
The glass-merchant demon, of petty ambition,
who fashions merely the craft-variations of his own family, stumbles.
He is consumed inwardly by envy of the rival gem of the lord of jewels, the <s>Kaustubha</s>,
which is effortlessly skilled in its setting. //
Where is the goddess <s>Durgā</s> (<s>Bhavānī</s>), the sister, who removes misfortune?
Where is the god <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the brother-in-law, friend of the distressed?
Where now is the wretchedness of seeking refuge in the ocean?
O <s>Maināka</s>, this should not be told to us by you! //
The lofty peak's self-height is in vain — it does not hold on
to the sun that desires to proceed to setting.
Praiseworthy is he — the lord of the <s>Maruts</s> (winds) — who, even with the mere quality of a lotus stalk,
out of fear of the demon, came and clung to it. //
His home is a cremation ground, his garment is elephant-skin,
his ointment is ash, and a bull is his vehicle.
O <s>Kubera</s>, lord of wealth, are you not ashamed
at this poverty of your dear friend? //
Power is not limited to one place; cessation is nowhere —
all states have their natural gradation firmly established.
The ocean, being drunk since the beginning of creation by the submarine fire,
was swallowed by <s>Agastya</s> in a single sip. //
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the blessed one, supports the entire earth;
him, the serpent [supports], and that [serpent] together with him, the ocean [supports].
The pot-born one (<s>Agastya</s>) drank even that, easily indeed —
truly, there is no limit to the greatness of the great. //
Placed upon the broad hip-slope of a young woman,
held firmly around the neck by the breadth of her arms,
pressed hard by the weight of her high, full breasts —
this pot enjoys the fruits of the cow-dung fire. //
If a dog, with an artificial mane tied on, its shoulder-area covered with flowing [locks],
is placed in the position of the lord of beasts —
how will it produce the roar of the king of deer (lion),
who is eager to split the frontal slopes of maddened elephants? //
He whose face alone — the source of splendor remaining even after all else —
makes the sharp-rayed moon into an object of eclipse;
if indeed his full body had been manifest,
what indeed, what indeed would <s>Rāhu</s> not have done then! //
Because your presence or absence, O parrot, is not known
due to the confusion of similarity with flowers, sprouts, and fruits —
therefore you do not abandon the pomegranate, out of desire for [its] fruit.
One distressed by [desire for] gain does not reckon the fault of degradation. //

children.text: varamiha ravitāpaiḥ kiṃ na śīrṇāsi gulme
children.translated_text: Would it not have been better, O <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine), to have withered in the shrub from the sun's heat,
or to have been burned entirely by forest fires,
than to be plucked by heartless crowds ignorant of stalk and leaf,
[and placed] among other flowers? //
Is this proper for one of purity, clearly of exalted wings,
ripened in fruit, fit to attain the love of virtues —
that you, O arrow, having approached the ear for a moment, then standing before another,
fall cruelly from afar and kill, O merciless one? //
That golden ornament, with dust clinging from falling to the ground of a king,
once the pride of a king's head, has been brought to such wretchedness
that, with discrimination obscured by the delusion of [being mistaken for] a clod of earth,
people, seeing it, avoid it out of fear of stubbing their feet! //
When birds are summoned, the mosquito who has not come is not barred from the front,

children.text: madhye vā dhuri vā vasaṃstṛṇamaṇirdhatte maṇīnāṃ rucam /
children.translated_text: nor from the middle or the lead — and the glass-bead, sitting [among them], assumes the radiance of gems.

children.text: khadyotopi na kampate pracalituṃ madhyepi tejasvināṃ
children.translated_text: Even the firefly does not hesitate to move about amid the luminous ones.
Fie upon the commonplace and the insensate, who, like a master, have not touched the inner truth! //
'If this is so, then the affinity with juiciness is [its] nature — why such dullness?
If there is indeed natural straightness, why such knottiness?
If the root is in the mud, why this scriptural fame of the lotus? If these are virtues,

children.text: kiṃ chidrāṇi sakhe mṛṇāla bhavatastattvaṃ na manyāmahe //
children.translated_text: then why the holes? O friend <s>mṛṇāla</s> (lotus fiber), we do not understand your true nature.' //

children.text: tvaṃ bhogī yadi kuṇḍalī yadi bhavāṃstvaṃ cedbhujaṃgaḥ sakhe
children.translated_text: 'You are an enjoyer, if a ring-bearer, if you are a serpent, friend,

children.text: dhatse cenmukuṭaṃ saratnamuraga svastyastu te kiṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: if you wear a jeweled crown, O snake — may it be well with you, but what of it?

children.text: asthāne yadi kañcukaṃ tyajasi tannāsmākamatra spṛhā
children.translated_text: If you shed your skin at the wrong time — we have no envy of that.',

children.text: kiṃ tu krūraviṣolkayā dahasi yadbhrātaḥ ka eṣa grahaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'But that you burn people with the fire of your cruel poison, brother — what kind of seizure is this?' //

children.text: maulau sanmaṇayo gṛhaṃ giriguhā tyāgaḥ kilātmatvaco
children.translated_text: 'On the head, fine gems; the home, a mountain cave; the sacrifice, of one's own skin;
and livelihood effortlessly by the breezes — such is the conduct in one respect.',

children.text: anyatrānṛju vartma vāgvitasanā dṛṣṭau viṣaṃ dṛśyate
children.translated_text: 'In another: a crooked path, speech devoid of garments, poison seen in the gaze —

children.text: yādṛktāmanu dīpako jvalati kiṃ bhoginsakhe kinvidam //
children.translated_text: how does the lamp blaze following you, O serpent-friend? What indeed is this?' //
'This one has many mouths — his great strength is indeed well known;

children.text: kadrvāḥ prākprasavoyamatra kupite cintyaṃ yathedaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: this is the firstborn of <s>Kadrū</s> — when he is angry, the world must think thus.'

children.text: trailokyādbhutamīdṛśaṃ tu caritaṃ śoṣasya yenāsya sā
children.translated_text: 'But this most wondrous conduct in the three worlds: by [<s>Garuḍa</s>'s] drying up,
that stain of being a poison-bearer has been wiped away, as it were, even from knowledge.' //
What use is that golden mountain (<s>Meru</s>) or the silver mountain (<s>Kailāsa</s>),
in whose shelter trees are merely trees?
We esteem <s>Malaya</s> (the Sandalwood mountain) alone, in whose shelter
even <s>śāhoṭa</s>, <s>nimba</s> (neem), and <s>kuṭaja</s> (wild jasmine) become sandalwood trees. //
Those whose arrows are smeared with poison, whose treachery is but little regarded,

children.text: lokaṃ hantumanāgasaṃ dvirasanā randhreṣu ye jāgrati /
children.translated_text: those two-tongued ones who watch for weak points to kill the innocent world —
even those serpents, foolish in [distinguishing] good and bad, bear gems upon their heads.
By the propriety of the virtuous, there is never any fall — enough of worry! //

children.text: tatpratyastratayā dhṛto na tu kṛtaḥ samyaksvatantro bhayāt-
children.translated_text: He was kept as a counter-weapon, but not truly made independent, out of fear
that, being secure, he would strike back at them — thus he was not nourished as desired.

children.text: saṃśuṣyanvṛṣadaṃśa eṣa kurutāṃ mūkaḥ sthitopyatra kiṃ
children.translated_text: 'Let this <s>vṛṣadaṃśa</s> (scorpion), drying up and standing here mute, do [what he will] —
what more [need be said]? Now in the householder's home, the thieves are rats.' //

children.text: svātmīyānna dadāsi cetphaṇamaṇīnmā dāḥ parārthaṃ parair-
children.translated_text: 'If you do not give your own hood-gems, then do not — [but] for the sake of others, by others —
that you block whatever little is deposited, what is this, O one of evil intent, like a [guardian of] treasure?'
'That much is enough [about you]. But I ask another thing: why, alas,
do you burn this world with hissings heavy with the force of poison-fire?' //

children.text: niḥsārāḥ sutarāṃ laghuprakṛtayo yogyā na kārye kvacic-
children.translated_text: Those utterly without substance, of light nature, fit for no task whatsoever —
those who are drying today, old grass-parts and the like, having attained independence —
alas! By this wind, devoid of inner substance,
see! — being extremely fickle, [they] are raised to the sky on the path of the great! //

children.text: ye jātyā laghavaḥ sadaiva gaṇanāṃ yātā na ye kutracit-
children.translated_text: Those who are light by birth, who have never anywhere been counted,
daily trampled underfoot, long hidden on the ground —
tossed up by the fickle-minded wind, see! In the sky, O friend,
these dust-particles stand atop the lofty mountains! //

children.text: anīrṣyāḥ śrotāro mama vacasi cedvacmi tadahaṃ
children.translated_text: If the listeners of my words are free from envy, then I say this:
one should fear much more from one's own side than from the powerful adversary.
When the directions are invaded by darkness, even those having the age of radiance

children.text: svaśaktyā bhāsante divasakṛti satyeva na punaḥ //
children.translated_text: shine by their own power — but when the sun exists, they do not. //

children.text: sāṃmukhyaṃ vastujātaṃ nayati nanu cidīśasya yaddarśanāḍhyaṃ
children.translated_text: The pair of eyes — rich in vision — brings all things into the presence of the lord of consciousness, is that not so?
These [eyes] are said to be pure, and thus, abandoning contact with other limbs,
the nose — delightful to the lineage, devoted to fragrance — in the middle of the eyes,

children.text: nityaṃ līnaṃ na cāsminmṛgasi nayanayoḥ śvāsamāmuñca khinne //
children.translated_text: ever nestled [there] — O deer, do not breathe a sigh upon the distressed eyes. //
From his mouth, how much [is it]? — A drop of water on a lotus leaf
That fool thought it was a pearl released [by the swan] — but hearing what came next,
as it was slowly offered forth, dissolving in the delicate play of the fingertips,
when it flew away — 'Alas!' — he sleeps no more day after day, consumed by inner grief. //
He sits right there in the lake — ah, what contentment grips this swan!

children.text: haṃsasyāsya manāṅna dhāvati matiḥ śrīdhāmni padme kvacit /
children.translated_text: His mind does not run in the least toward the lotus, the abode of <s>Śrī</s> (fortune).
'He sleeps and even when awakened does not stir from there — so long let us wait

children.text: velāmityuṣasi priyā madhulihaḥ soḍhuṃ tu eva kṣamāḥ //
children.translated_text: for the [right] moment,' say the beloved honey-bees — but they are quite able to endure the wait! //
Saying 'We live on air,' the serpents were reassured and consumed entirely by them.
They in turn were devoured by the peacocks, [who observe] the severe vow of drinking only cloud-drops.
Those too were destroyed by hunters, fierce, wearing leather garments.

children.text: dambhasya sphuritaṃ vidannapi jano jālmo guṇānīhate //
children.translated_text: Even knowing the manifestation of deceit, the foolish world pursues [false] virtues! //
One eye of another was closed — meanwhile the other was opened.
As fate stumbled on its own path, its hand was grasped by others.
And this world was delivered from the calamity of blindness, the slaughter of sight.
It was fitting, O woodcutter, that you felled that mango grove grown dark [with density]! //

children.text: ūḍhā yena mahādhuraḥ suviṣame mārge sadaikākinā
children.translated_text: He who alone bore the great burden on the most difficult path,

children.text: soḍho yena kadācideva na nije goṣṭhenyaśauṇḍadhvaniḥ /
children.translated_text: he who never once tolerated the sound of [another's] arrogance in his own stable,
he who was the ornament of the herd of cattle — now, alas,
the shame! — the sale of that white bull, grown old, is being announced! //
That the frog, croaking harshly in anger, into the mouth of the black serpent,
raised its hand, fearlessly, to deliver a slap on the ear,
and that the cobra stood there with face lowered, covering its eyes —
all this is the playful sport of some blessed lord whose counselor is poison! //
Its dwelling is always at a sacred ford; its nature is exceedingly gentle and innocent;
its sustenance, by fate, falls into its mouth — pure drops of water from the sky.

children.text: itthaṃ sarvaṃ vilokya prakaṭamiha time mugdhalokena loke
children.translated_text: Having observed all this openly here in the world, the naive public

children.text: sādhutvaṃ darśitaṃ te bahirabahiramī kaṇṭakāḥ kena dṛṣṭāḥ //
children.translated_text: attributed saintliness to you — but who has seen these inner thorns of yours? //
Its bow is stretched like the mouth of death; these arrows are like venomous serpents.

children.text: śikṣā sāpi jitārjunā pratibhayaṃ sarvāṅganimnā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Its skill too surpasses <s>Arjuna</s>'s; its gait is terrifying, crouching with all limbs low.

children.text: antaḥ krauryamaho śaṭhasya madhuraṃ hā hāri geyaṃ mukhe
children.translated_text: Cruelty within — ah, but on the lips of this deceitful one, sweet, captivating song!

children.text: vyādhasyāsya yathā bhaviṣyati tathā manye vanaṃ nirmṛgam //
children.translated_text: I reckon that as this hunter shall go, so shall the forest be emptied of deer. //
Fie upon the greatness of the sky — let its lofty station fall to pieces!
Let the blameworthy course of fate go to destruction — let that void have its emptiness!
For the sky did not extend a hand to steady a friend

children.text: mitrasyāpi nirāśrayasya na kṛtaṃ dhṛtyai karālambanam //
children.translated_text: who raised his arms in desperation, whose glory was lost, who was weary and afflicted, and without refuge. //

children.text: digdāhaikarate vanāntakara te jvālā na me rocate
children.translated_text: You, O [forest fire], devoted solely to burning the horizons, destroyer of forests — your flame does not please me.

children.text: dugdhaṃ svāśrayamudyatasya bhavato necchanti vṛddhiṃ janāḥ /
children.translated_text: People do not wish prosperity for one who burns his own refuge and then ventures forth.
You were created by the wicked Creator to shatter the roots of this mountain.

children.text: ko vā na tvayi śaṅkate khala jagatkhedāvahe dāva he //
children.translated_text: O villain, O forest fire, bringer of suffering to the world — who does not fear you? //

children.text: kṣutkṣāmeṇa kathaṃ kathaṃcidaniśaṃ gātraṃ kṛśaṃ bibhratā
children.translated_text: Emaciated by hunger, bearing a thin body somehow ceaselessly,
wandering from house to house among householders, begging for scraps of leftovers —
having obtained a piece of bone fallen by fate, thinking this entire triple world empty —

children.text: manvāno dhigaho sa eva saramāputrodya siṃhāyate //
children.translated_text: shame! That very son of <s>Saramā</s> (a dog) now acts the lion today! //
A cow's bone, meatless, smeared with dried sinew and fat —

children.text: śvā labdhā paritoṣameti na tu tattasya kṣudhaḥ śāntaye /
children.translated_text: a dog, having obtained it, is pleased — but it does not appease his hunger.
<s>Siṃha</s> (the lion) rejects even a jackal that has come to his lap, and slays the elephant.

children.text: sarvaḥ kṛchragatopi vāñchati janaḥ sattvānurūpaṃ phalam //
children.translated_text: Everyone, even in dire straits, desires a reward befitting their nature. //

children.text: kāluṣyaṃ payasāṃ vilokya śanakairuḍḍīya haṃsā gatā
children.translated_text: Seeing the muddiness of the waters, the swans slowly flew away and departed.
The lotuses, their filaments battered by rain, their beauty unexpanded, sank into the water.
That path of entry to happiness in all seasons was covered with fresh grass.

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ tādṛgapi svabhāvavimalaṃ vṛdchyaiva naṣṭaṃ saraḥ //
children.translated_text: Alas, even that lake, pure by nature, was ruined by the rains! //
For those whose minds are awakened by the bliss of contentment, [<s>Meru</s>] is no different from clay.
But for those whose minds are confounded by greed for wealth — it is far from [satisfying] men.

children.text: itthaṃ kasya kṛte kṛtaḥ sa vidhinā tādṛkpadaṃ saṃpadāṃ
children.translated_text: Thus, for whose sake was that station of riches created by the Creator?
<s>Meru</s>, whose golden glory is complete in itself alone, does not please me. //
The mixing up of goods, high and low; below, the depositing of seeds of those whose hopes are shattered,
and themselves seeking out crevices like their own flaws —
by fearless mice, forming battle-arrays, finding the house empty while a naive child slept —

children.text: śūnyaṃ prāpya nivāsamākhubhiraho kiṃ kiṃ na yadyatkṛtam //
children.translated_text: alas, what indeed have they not done! //
At the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), when the great elements have dissolved into one another as if in fear,

children.text: kalpānte parameka eva sa taruḥ skandhoccayairjṛmbhate /
children.translated_text: that one tree alone extends itself with its massed trunks.
Having placed the three worlds in the hollow of his belly, the god reclines upon it,
playing upon its branch-tip like a child at water-play, languidly. // [Of <s>Trivikrama</s>]
The beloved of the god <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), whose mind is devoted to benefiting the three worlds,
born in the mountain lineage, delighting the gods with her chosen boons,
<s>Ambikā</s> (the Mother Goddess), devoted to fulfilling even the wishes of barbarians, of her own abode —

children.text: vindhyasyonnatimātanoti na nijāṃ daivasya kīdṛgbalam //bhā. amṛtadattasya
children.translated_text: extends the eminence of <s>Vindhya</s>, not her own — how mighty is the power of destiny! // [Of <s>Amṛtadatta</s>]

children.text: kiṃ tvaṃ hālika mūḍhadhīrhataphalaṃ mā mā kṛthā lāṅgalaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Why, O foolish-minded ploughman, do you persist? Do not, do not take up the plough!

children.text: kṣetraṃ naiva bhavatyadhaḥ kaṭhinatā naivātra dṛṣṭā tvayā /
children.translated_text: This is no field — have you not seen the hardness below?

children.text: ullekhopi na jāyatetra virama kleśaḥ phalaṃ kevalaṃ
children.translated_text: Not even a scratch is produced here — desist! Toil alone is the result.

children.text: nirbījā bahavo gatāśca satataṃ dṛṣṭāḥ śrutā vā na kim //kasyāpi
children.translated_text: Many have gone away fruitless and seedless — have you not seen or heard?' // [Of someone]
'What is this delusion of yours, O wind? You carry to the sky a mass of dust
born from the refuse-heap, establishing it in the firmament that is frequented by hosts of the brilliant!
When it is raised up, let the trouble to people's eye-paths be set aside —

children.text: kenopāyena sahyo vapuṣi malinatādoṣa eṣa tvayaiva //bhā. amṛtadattasya
children.translated_text: by what means is even the flaw of dirtiness on your own body to be endured?' // [Of <s>Amṛtadatta</s>]

children.text: jātaḥ kūrmaḥ sa ekaḥ pṛthubhuvanabharāyārpitaṃ yena pṛṣṭhaṃ
children.translated_text: That one tortoise alone was born, who offered his back to bear the weight of the broad world.

children.text: ślāghyaṃ janma dhruvasya bhramati niyamitaṃ yatra tejasvicakram /
children.translated_text: Praiseworthy is the birth of <s>Dhruva</s> (the Pole Star), where the wheel of luminaries revolves in fixed course.
With wings rendered useless, unable to serve others' welfare — neither above nor below —
other creatures, like gnats inside the shell of the cosmic egg, are born and perish! // [Of someone]
'Why do you screech so harshly in the ears, O enemy of elephants?
O one ignorant of your own intellect — is nothing known [to you]?
With skull cracked open by the blow of a sharp-tipped tusk,
O mosquito, a herd of elephants drowned in the aperture of [your] throat!' // [Of someone]
'I am a fierce one, uprooting bank-dwelling trees with my crooked course! —

children.text: mā garvīḥ saritaḥ pravāha jaladhiṃ prakṣobhayāmīti bhoḥ /
children.translated_text: Do not be proud, O river-current, saying "I shall agitate the ocean!"

children.text: svāṃ sattāṃ yadi vāñchasi bhrama maruṣvevāḥsva tatraiva vā
children.translated_text: If you desire your own existence, wander in the deserts, or remain right there.',
'For far off is the submarine fire — and entering here, you are drunk up by the great beings!' //
'Steadfastness! O lofty-peaked one, shore-mountain resorted to for the world's stability!

children.text: dūrātpreraṇayā kalāvata imaṃ krāntuṃ jalānāṃ pate /
children.translated_text: O lord of waters, do you vainly desire to cross over the skillful one by pushing from afar?

children.text: mithyā vāñchasi kiṃ tatastava paraṃ syādratnasattvakṣayo
children.translated_text: Thereby your chief wealth of gems and creatures would perish.
Surely, upon striking his foot-sole, you would at last roll away as mere [froth] at his feet!' //
You ceaselessly rock the sky-sun in your lap,
and the host of stars, and the moon, and likewise the other
luminaries such as blazing lightning — O virtuous one,
yet it is wondrous that you still do not abandon your inner blindness! //
This is that <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), whose self-restraint is renowned in the three worlds —
yet now, tormented by separation, he bears a woman in his body.

children.text: anena kila nirjitā vayamiti priyāyāḥ karaṃ
children.translated_text: 'By him, we have been conquered indeed' — pressing the hand of his beloved
with his own hand, <s>Smara</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>, the god of love), laughing, triumphs! //
Those [arrows of <s>Kāma</s>] that are shot from the bow of the eyebrows, stealing the sky-beauty of the blue lotus and the bee —
those that are like intoxicated black deer, heart-piercing, with cruel star-tipped barbs —
those long side-glances feathered at their nocks, uneven with the poison of a smile, thick-lashed —
may the women's sidelong glances, the arrows of the five-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>), conqueror of the three worlds, of supreme power, protect you! //

children.text: gaccha gacchasi cetkānta panthānaḥ santu te śivāḥ /
children.translated_text: Go, go if you must, O beloved — may your paths be auspicious!

children.text: mamāpi janma tatraiva bhūyādyatra gato bhavān //
children.translated_text: May my next birth too be in that very place where you have gone. //
